entries.definitionCN: 身体不大舒服的

entries.definition: weak or ill, often mildly and over time
entries.definitionCN: 身体欠佳的；抱病的

normalIntro.en: Sickish is sick made small by -ish: the same English word with a dimmer switch attached.
normalIntro.cn: sickish 是被 -ish 调暗了的 sick：同一个英语词，加了个调光开关。

normal.en: The suffix -ish often means somewhat, as in reddish and oldish.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ish 常表示「有点儿」，如 reddish、oldish。

normal.en: Sickish is therefore somewhat sick, not seriously ill.
normal.cn: 所以 sickish 就是「有点儿病」，而不是重病。

normal.en: Sickly is stronger and suggests continuing poor health, while sickish is mild and passing.
normal.cn: sickly 程度更重，暗示长期的体弱；sickish 轻微且短暂。

normal.en: Feel sickish is the usual verb phrase for quiet nausea.
normal.cn: feel sickish 是表示轻微反胃的常用动词搭配。

normal.en: Sickish also tints colours and smells, the way -ish tints other words.
normal.cn: sickish 也能修饰颜色和气味，正如 -ish 可修饰许多词。

abstract.en: Picture someone gripping a rail and breathing slowly while the floor seems to tilt.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人抓住栏杆慢慢呼吸，脚下的地面好像在倾斜。

abstract.en: See a sick person crossed out with a light pencil line, not a heavy one.
abstract.cn: 想象用铅笔轻轻划掉一个病人图像，而不是重重涂掉。

abstract.en: Think of a wall painted a dull yellow that makes the room feel wrong.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵刷成暗黄色的墙，让整个房间透着不对劲。

examples.en: He felt sickish after the long climb and leaned against the wall.
examples.cn: 长途攀登之后他觉得有点恶心，便靠着墙。

examples.en: The air in the cellar was sickish and damp.
examples.cn: 地窖里的空气潮湿，还有点令人难受。

examples.en: She felt sickish for a day but never had a fever.
examples.cn: 她难受了一天，却始终没有发烧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四个一席」——四个人挤一席，闷得人有点发晕想吐；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 seoc（生病的）+ 古英语后缀 -isc（具有……性质；有点儿）→ 中古英语 sik → 近代英语 sick + -ish = sickish，核心义「病得不厉害的半病状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Sickish begins as a light bodily nauseousness, spreads to a person only half unwell, then to a quality that looks unhealthy and finally to things that mildly disturb the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: sickish 先指身体的轻度反胃，再指人处于半病未病的状态，然后指外观上不健康的性质，最后扩展到让人心里微微不适的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person steadies themselves against a wall, pale and queasy, but still standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人扶着墙站稳，脸色发白、胃里翻腾，但还站得住。

branches.en: The stomach gives the first, most physical sense.
branches.cn: 胃部反应给出最具体的第一义项。

branches.en: The half state of the body is the everyday adjective sense.
branches.cn: 身体的半病状态是日常的形容词义项。

branches.en: The softener can attach an unhealthy tint to colours and smells.
branches.cn: 这个减弱后缀能把病态色调附着到颜色和气味上。

branches.en: Beyond the body, it names ideas and behaviour that faintly disgust.
branches.cn: 超出身体范围后，它可以指让人微微反感的想法与行为。

branches.en: All three share the same moderation: not fully sick, only slightly off.
branches.cn: 三者共享同一种「轻微」：不是真病，只是有点不对劲。

intro.en: Sickish is a simple English structure, the base adjective sick plus the native suffix -ish, and the same suffix builds many softened adjectives.
intro.cn: sickish 的构造很简单，就是基础形容词 sick 加本族后缀 -ish，而同一个后缀还构成许多「减弱」形容词。

latinIntro.en: The root is not Latin but Old English, so the Latin parallels here are the quality endings and illness words that do a similar job.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的根不是拉丁语，而是古英语，所以这里的拉丁对照是作用相近的性质词尾与疾病词。

items.example: Sick is an old native English adjective.
items.exampleCN: sick 是古老的英语本族形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ish softens the adjective it follows.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 会弱化它前面的形容词。

items.example: Sickish adds -ish to a native stem.
items.exampleCN: sickish 是在本族词干后加 -ish。

items.example: The suffix -ness turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成名词。

items.example: The suffix -ly here makes a quality adjective, not an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 -ly 造成表示性质的形容词，而非副词。

items.example: Sickness names the state itself.
items.exampleCN: sickness 指病症本身。

items.example: The suffix -en forms a verb of change.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -en 构成表示变化的动词。

items.example: Reddish shows -ish in its purely colour sense.
items.exampleCN: reddish 展示了 -ish 纯表颜色的一面。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms sickishness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 sickishness。

latinEntries.meaning: full of, having the quality of
latinEntries.meaningCN: 充满……的；具有……性质的词尾

definition_zh: 午睡；午后小憩；午休时段
definition_en: a short rest or sleep taken in the early afternoon, especially in hot countries, or the period when this is done
core_image: 正午的日影最短，街边的百叶窗全都放下，整座小镇安静入睡
scene: 南方小城的午后，店铺一块块拉下卷帘，街上几乎没有行人。After lunch the whole office takes a siesta and the phones stop ringing.
sceneCN: 这里 siesta 是「午睡」（第 1 个义项：午后的小睡）；句意为午饭后整个办公室都在午睡，电话也不再响。图中可辨识物件：卷帘门、百叶窗、石墙、晾着的床单。

pos.zh: 午睡；午后小憩；午休时段

derivatives.zh: siesta 的复数形式，指多次或不同类型的午睡
siesta 加 -ing 构成的分词，义为「正在午睡」

senses.title: A short afternoon sleep
senses.definition: a brief sleep taken after the midday meal, especially in countries where the afternoons are hot
senses.definitionCN: 午饭之后所做的一次短暂睡眠，尤其在午后炎热的地区
senses.example: We took a siesta under the shade of the olive tree.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在橄榄树的荫下睡了个午觉。
senses.why: Latin sexta hora meant the sixth hour of the day, counted from sunrise, so the word began as a time and later named the rest taken at that time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sexta hora 意为日间的第六个小时，从日出算起，所以这个词本是一个时刻，后来才指在那个时刻所做的休息。

senses.title: The quiet midday period
senses.definition: the part of the early afternoon when shops close, streets empty and people rest
senses.definitionCN: 午后初段商店关门、街道空荡、人们休息的那段时间
senses.example: The market empties during the siesta and reopens around five.
senses.exampleCN: 市场在午休时段空无一人，大约五点钟才重新开门。
senses.why: Because an entire town shuts down at that hour, the hour itself was given the name of the sleep.
senses.whyCN: 由于整座城镇在那个时刻都歇业，这个时段本身也被冠以小睡之名。

senses.title: A nap as a habit
senses.definition: the midday rest as a cultural practice, especially associated with Spain and the warmer countries of southern Europe and Latin America
senses.definitionCN: 作为一种文化习惯的午间休息，尤与西班牙及南欧、拉丁美洲较热的地区相联系
senses.example: The siesta is less common in Spain than visitors expect.
senses.exampleCN: 在西班牙，午睡并不像游客以为的那样普遍。
senses.why: A repeated practice turns the single nap into a social custom, so the word can stand for the habit itself.
senses.whyCN: 一种反复出现的行为会把单次小睡变成社会习俗，于是这个词也能代表这种习惯本身。

senses.title: To nap in the afternoon
senses.definition: to take a short rest after lunch, used as a verb in informal English
senses.definitionCN: 午饭后小睡片刻，在非正式英语中作动词使用
senses.example: They siesta for half an hour before the second round of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 在第二轮会谈开始前，他们会午睡半小时。
senses.why: English readily turns names of restful activities into verbs, so the Spanish loan became a verb meaning to take such a rest.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表示休息活动的名词直接用作动词，因此这个西班牙语借词也成了「睡这种觉」的动词。

intro.en: Siesta comes from Spanish siesta, which goes back to Latin sexta hora, the sixth hour, counted from sunrise and so falling around midday.
intro.cn: siesta 来自西班牙语 siesta，可上溯到拉丁语 sexta hora（第六个小时），从日出算起，大约正是正午前后。

items.en: Sexta is the feminine form of sextus, sixth, from sex, six, the same numeral root as six and sextet.
items.cn: sexta 是 sextus（第六）的阴性形式，来自 sex（六），与 six、sextet 同属一个数词词根。

items.en: The Roman day was counted from sunrise, so hora sexta was the sixth hour, the hottest part of the day around noon.
items.cn: 罗马人以日出开始计时，所以 hora sexta 是第六个小时，即一天中最热、约在正午的时段。

items.en: Church Latin also used sexta for the midday prayer service, one of the canonical hours kept each day.
items.cn: 教会拉丁语也用 sexta 指正午的日课经，即每日必行的定时祈祷之一。

items.en: Spanish borrowed the hour as siesta and added the idea of resting through the heat of the afternoon.
items.cn: 西班牙语把这个时刻借入为 siesta，并加上了「在午后酷热中歇息」的含义。

items.en: English took siesta in the seventeenth century from travellers describing daily life in Spain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪从讲述西班牙日常生活的旅行者那里借入 siesta。

note.en: Siesta is the Spanish midday hour at rest, so its look-alikes are the time and rest words it travelled beside, and its near meanings are naps of every other name.
note.cn: siesta 是西班牙语里歇息的正午时光，所以形近词是它一路同行的「时刻」与「休息」词，近义词则是名字各异的各类小睡。

entries.definition: an Italian name for the same midday rest
entries.definitionCN: 意大利语中同一午间休息的词

entries.definition: the midday prayer service in church tradition
entries.definitionCN: 教会传统中的午时祈祷

entries.definition: a Spanish festival or holiday
entries.definitionCN: 西班牙式节日或庆典（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a short sleep, especially in the day
entries.definitionCN: 小睡；打盹

entries.definition: a light, brief sleep
entries.definitionCN: 打瞌睡；微睡

entries.definition: a period of relaxing without work
entries.definitionCN: 休息；歇息

normalIntro.en: Siesta is a borrowed time word: it began as the sixth hour and turned into the nap taken then.
normalIntro.cn: siesta 是一个借来的「时刻」词：本义是第六个小时，后来变成在那个时刻睡的那一觉。

normal.en: Sexta hora in Latin means the sixth hour after sunrise, close to noon.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 sexta hora 意为日出后的第六个小时，接近正午。

normal.en: Sextus and sex are the Latin words for sixth and six, so siesta shares its root with six.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 sextus、sex 分别是「第六」与「六」，所以 siesta 与 six 同根。

normal.en: Spanish kept the midday rest and passed the word on to English travellers.
normal.cn: 西班牙语保留了这项午间休息，并把词传给了英语旅行者。

normal.en: Siesta commonly follows take or have: take a siesta, have a siesta.
normal.cn: siesta 常跟在 take 或 have 之后：take a siesta、have a siesta。

normal.en: Siesta is milder in force than nap: nap is a plain short sleep, siesta adds the hot-afternoon setting.
normal.cn: siesta 的语气比 nap 更具文化色彩：nap 只是普通小睡，siesta 带上了炎热午后的场景。

abstract.en: Picture a sunlit square at noon with every shutter pulled down and not a soul walking.
abstract.cn: 想象正午阳光下的广场，所有百叶窗都放下，路上一个人也没有。

abstract.en: See a café chair tipped against the wall while the owner dozes in the shade.
abstract.cn: 想象咖啡椅斜靠门边，店主在阴凉里打盹。

abstract.en: Think of a town whose clock stops for an hour every afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇的钟，每天下午都会停走一个小时。

examples.en: We left the beach at noon, had a siesta, and went out again at four.
examples.cn: 我们正午离开海滩，睡了个午觉，四点钟又出门了。

examples.en: The office empties during the siesta and fills again at half past four.
examples.cn: 午休时办公室空荡荡的，四点半又坐满了人。

examples.en: Visitors often expect every shop to close for a siesta.
examples.cn: 游客常常以为每家店都会为午睡关门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歇一下他」——正午太热，让干活的人歇一下他，就是午睡；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sexta hora（第六个小时，从日出起算的午后正午）→ 教会拉丁语 sexta（午时祈祷）→ 西班牙语 siesta（午间休息）→ 英语 siesta，核心义「正午时分的歇息」。

sensesIntro.en: Siesta starts as the hot hour at noon, then means the sleep taken in that hour, the quiet period itself and finally a verb for napping.
sensesIntro.cn: siesta 先指正午那个炎热的小时，进而指在这个小时里睡的一觉，再指这段安静的时段，最后成为表示「小睡」的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: at noon all shutters come down, the sun stands overhead and the whole town sleeps for an hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：正午时分百叶窗齐齐落下，太阳悬在头顶，整座小镇睡上一个小时。

branches.en: The nap taken at that hour is the core sense.
branches.cn: 在那个时刻睡的这一觉是核心义项。

branches.en: The silent hour of closed shops is the time sense.
branches.cn: 商店关门、街道无声的那段时间是时段义项。

branches.en: When the hour is kept every day, the nap becomes a custom with a regional name.
branches.cn: 当这个时刻天天重复，小睡便成为带有地域色彩的习惯。

branches.en: English turns the rest into a verb, as it does with many activity nouns.
branches.cn: 英语像对待许多活动名词那样，把这次休息变成了动词。

branches.en: The three share the midday setting, though one is time, one habit and one action.
branches.cn: 三者共享正午场景，但一个是时段，一个是习惯，一个是动作。

intro.en: Siesta is a borrowing from Spanish, and the English forms around it are plurals and verb forms rather than new derivations.
intro.cn: siesta 是从西班牙语借来的词，英语围绕它的形式主要是复数和动词变化，而不是新的派生词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin behind siesta is the ordinal and numeral sexta and sex, still visible in English words about the number six.
latinIntro.cn: siesta 背后的拉丁语是序数词 sexta 与数词 sex，在英语里与「六」有关的词中仍能看到它们。

items.example: Sexta names the sixth hour of the day.
items.exampleCN: sexta 指一天中的第六个小时。

items.example: Sex is the numeral behind sexta and sextus.
items.exampleCN: sex 是 sexta 与 sextus 背后的数词。

items.example: Spanish siesta shortened the Latin phrase.
items.exampleCN: 西班牙语 siesta 缩减了这个拉丁短语。

items.example: Siestas are common in small towns here.
items.exampleCN: 这里的乡镇常有人午睡。

items.example: Sext survives in church usage.
items.exampleCN: sext 仍保留在教会的用语中。

items.example: The Latin six root also builds sextet.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语「六」的词根也构成 sextet。

items.example: Sesta is the Italian form of the idea.
items.exampleCN: sesta 是这个概念的意大利语形式。

items.example: Siested forms borrow the regular English past tense.
items.exampleCN: 名词作动词后，按英语规则加 -ed 构成过去式。

definition_zh: 筛；筛选；细查；遣词中逐渐传开
definition_en: to pass something through a sieve or screen, or to examine material or information carefully in order to separate what matters from what does not
core_image: 面粉倒进细筛，颗粒留在网上，细粉落进盆里
scene: 考古队员把刚挖出的泥土一层层筛过，想找出陶片和炭粒。At the site, the students sift the freshly dug soil to find potsherds and charcoal.
sceneCN: 这里 sift 是「筛」（第 1 个义项：让散粒通过筛网分离粗细）；句意：在发掘现场，学生们筛新挖出的泥土，寻找陶片和炭粒。

pos.zh: 细细筛下来；逐渐落到某处

collocations.phrase: sift the facts from the rumours

derivatives.zh: 由 sift 加 -er 构成，指「筛子；筛分者」
由 sift 加 -ing 构成，指「筛分；筛查过程」
与 sift 同源的近义词，义为「筛子；筛网」

senses.title: To pass loose material through a sieve
senses.definition: to put flour, sand, soil, or another loose material through a sieve or screen so that large pieces stay behind
senses.definitionCN: 把面粉、沙子、泥土等松散材料放入筛网，使粗大颗粒留在网上
senses.example: Sift the flour twice before you make the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 做蛋糕前把面粉过筛两遍。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to sieve, and the sifting basket is the picture of separating fine from coarse.
senses.whyCN: 古英语本义就是「过筛」，而筛篮的画面正是一张网上留下粗粒、落下细粉，所以这个义项最直接。

senses.title: To examine material carefully to find what matters
senses.definition: to look through a mass of papers, records, or objects carefully, searching for something useful or important
senses.definitionCN: 仔细翻看大量文件、记录或物品，从中寻找有用或重要的东西
senses.example: She sifted through the archives for old photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 她在档案里仔细翻找旧照片。
senses.why: By the sixteenth century the sieve was applied to thoughts and words, and later to piles of records that must be worked through.
senses.whyCN: 到了十六世纪，筛子这个工具被用来「筛」想法和话语，后来就引申为把成堆材料一筐筐翻查一遍。

senses.title: To separate good from bad by judgment
senses.definition: to judge a group of people, ideas, or results and keep only those that are right or useful
senses.definitionCN: 对一群人、一批想法或结果作出判断，只保留正确或有用的部分
senses.example: Editors sift hundreds of applications to choose a few trainees.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑们从几百份申请中筛选出几名实习生。
senses.why: The screen does the same job as the sieve, keeping the valuable pieces while the rest falls away.
senses.whyCN: 筛网和筛子的作用一样：有价值的留下，其余的漏掉，所以筛选和甄别都带着「过网」的意味。

senses.title: To examine evidence by analysis
senses.definition: to compare data or evidence point by point so that the truth becomes clear
senses.definitionCN: 把数据或证据逐条比对，使真相显现出来
senses.example: Scientists sift the data before drawing a conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家在下结论之前先梳理数据。
senses.why: Sifting sorts grains by size, and analysis sorts facts by weight and reliability.
senses.whyCN: 筛分按颗粒大小把谷物分开，分析则按分量与可靠程度把事实分开，动作结构完全一致。

senses.title: To fall gradually through the air
senses.definition: of light snow, dust, or fine particles, to come down slowly and continuously
senses.definitionCN: 指细雪、灰尘或微细颗粒缓缓地连续落下
senses.example: Fine snow sifted down on the empty street.
senses.exampleCN: 细雪纷纷落在空荡的街道上。
senses.why: Loose grains falling through a sieve look exactly like snow drifting slowly from the sky.
senses.whyCN: 松散的颗粒从筛子里漏下，样子就像雪花从天上一片片飘落，画面可以互相借用。

senses.title: To become known little by little
senses.definition: of news, information, or a rumour, to spread slowly to more and more people
senses.definitionCN: 指消息、信息或传言慢慢地传到越来越多的人那里
senses.example: Word of the scandal sifted out to the press.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻的消息渐渐传到了媒体那里。
senses.why: Information passing through many small openings reaches one person at a time, like grains leaving a sieve.
senses.whyCN: 信息从许多小孔里一点一点漏出去，一次只到一个人手上，正如谷物从筛孔里慢慢溜走。

senses.title: To cause harm to a group by going through it
senses.definition: chiefly in British English, of soldiers or attackers, to move through a group or area damaging or disturbing it
senses.definitionCN: 主要见于英式英语，指士兵或袭击者穿过一群人或一片地区，一路袭扰破坏
senses.example: The raiders sifted through the small villages on the peninsula.
senses.exampleCN: 劫掠者穿过半岛上的小村落，一路袭扰。
senses.why: This rare sense keeps the sieve image of passing through a body of people and letting damage fall on them.
senses.whyCN: 这个少见的义项保留了「穿过」的筛子意象：攻击者像细沙一样渗过人群，把麻烦撒进去。

intro.en: Sift comes from Old English siftan, to sieve, likely linked to the same Germanic family as sieve and the Latin verb secernere, to separate.
intro.cn: sift 来自古英语 siftan（过筛），一般认为与 sieve 同属日耳曼语族，语义上与拉丁语 secernere（分开、辨别）相通。

items.en: The verb is generally reconstructed from a Germanic root meaning to sieve, though the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词源于日耳曼语中表示「过筛」的词根，但具体重构形式仍存疑。

items.en: Siftan means to sieve at home and in the mill.
items.cn: 古英语 siftan 指在家中或磨坊里过筛。

items.en: Writers begin to sift thoughts, words, and evidence instead of flour.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，作家开始「筛」思想、言辞和证据，而不只是筛面粉。

items.en: Sift is used for snow drifting down and for rumours spreading slowly.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，sift 用于描写雪花飘落和传言慢慢传开。

items.en: In science and administration sifting means careful screening of data and applicants.
items.cn: 在现代科学与行政语境中，sift 指对数据和申请者进行细致的筛选。

note.en: Sift belongs to a small family of sieve and screen words, and its near meanings shift between sieving and sorting.
note.cn: sift 属于「筛与网」这组小词族，近义侧重在「过筛」与「分拣」之间摇摆。

entries.definition: a device or person that sifts
entries.definitionCN: 由 sift 加 -er 构成的派生词，义为「筛子；筛分者」

entries.definition: the act or result of sifting
entries.definitionCN: 由 sift 加 -ing 构成的派生词，义为「筛分；筛查过程」

entries.definition: to rest on a seat
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同，义为「坐」

entries.definition: to put something through a sieve
entries.definitionCN: 把东西过筛，与 sift 几乎同义

entries.definition: to test or check people or things before accepting them
entries.definitionCN: 筛检；审查，偏重资格核查

entries.definition: to remove unwanted parts by passing through a filter
entries.definitionCN: 过滤；滤除，强调去掉杂质

normalIntro.en: Sift keeps the picture of a hand shaking a fine sieve so that only the small, useful grains fall through.
normalIntro.cn: sift 一直保留着一个画面：一只手晃动细筛，只有细小有用的颗粒才漏下去。

normal.en: Sift the flour to make the cake lighter.
normal.cn: 把面粉过筛，蛋糕会更松软。

normal.en: To sift through documents is to read them all looking for one thing.
normal.cn: sift through 文件，就是把它们全读一遍，寻找某一样东西。

normal.en: To sift out errors is to keep them from reaching the final report.
normal.cn: sift out 错误，就是不让错误进到最终报告里。

normal.en: Compare sieve and sift: the same picture, one is a noun, the other a verb.
normal.cn: 对比 sieve 和 sift：画面相同，前者是名词（筛子），后者是动词（筛）。

normal.en: Scientists sift data before they publish a result.
normal.cn: 科学家会在发表结果之前先梳理数据。

abstract.en: Picture a baker shaking a sieve and watching fine flour drop.
abstract.cn: 想象一位面包师晃着筛子，看细粉簌簌落下。

abstract.en: Imagine a researcher turning page after page in a dusty office.
abstract.cn: 想象一位研究者在积灰的办公室里一页一页翻找资料。

abstract.en: Think of a hiring team crossing out most names and keeping a few.
abstract.cn: 想象招聘团队划掉大多数名字，只留下几个。

examples.en: The recipe says to sift the cocoa powder into the bowl.
examples.cn: 做法说明要把可可粉筛进碗里。

examples.en: Police sifted through hours of footage to find the van.
examples.cn: 警方翻查了数小时的监控录像，找那辆面包车。

examples.en: The committee sifted the proposals and kept only three.
examples.cn: 委员会筛选了提案，只留下三份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「细粉」——sift 就是筛出细粉；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 siftan（过筛），一般认为属日耳曼语族「筛」词根，与 sieve（筛子）同源；核心义「让细的漏过，粗的留下」，由此延伸出「筛选、细查、飘落、传开」。

sensesIntro.en: Sift starts with a literal sieve, then moves to looking through records, judging what to keep, analysing evidence, drifting down, spreading slowly, and one rare military sense.
sensesIntro.cn: sift 从字面过筛出发，依次延伸为翻查材料、甄别取舍、梳理证据、缓缓飘落、慢慢传开，另有一个少见的军事义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flour shaken through a fine sieve, coarse grains left on the mesh.
core.cn: 核心意象：面粉在细筛上晃动，粗粒留在网面，细粉落下。

branches.en: Passing loose material through a sieve is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 把松散材料过筛是字面义项。

branches.en: Looking through records borrows the same sieve picture.
branches.cn: 翻查成堆材料借用了同一个筛子画面。

branches.en: Screening people and analysing evidence are judgments made with a mental sieve.
branches.cn: 筛选人员与梳理证据都是用心里的筛子作出的判断。

branches.en: Falling particles and spreading rumour both move through many small openings.
branches.cn: 落下的颗粒与传开的传言都从许多小孔慢慢通过。

branches.en: The rare raiding sense keeps the idea of passing through a group.
branches.cn: 少见的袭扰义项保留了「从人群中穿过」的意象。

intro.en: Sift is a short Germanic verb with no Latin prefix, but it shares its sieve picture with Latin forms of separating and examining.
intro.cn: sift 是简短的日耳曼语动词，不带拉丁语前缀，但它的「筛分」画面与拉丁语中表示分开、检查的词形相通。

latinIntro.en: Latin words such as cribrum, a sieve, and secernere, to separate, express the same act with different roots.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cribrum（筛子）与 secernere（分开、辨别）用不同的词根表达同样的动作。

items.example: Sift is the plain verb for using a sieve.
items.exampleCN: sift 是表示「用筛子」的普通动词。

items.meaning: a person or tool that does something
items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的工具或人的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms sifter.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 sifter。

items.example: A sifter is the tool used for sifting.
items.exampleCN: sifter 就是过筛用的工具。

items.example: Sifting is the act itself.
items.exampleCN: sifting 是筛的动作本身。

items.meaning: having been passed through a sieve
items.example: Sifted flour is finer flour.
items.exampleCN: sifted 形容过筛后面粉更细。

items.meaning: a tool with holes for separating
items.example: Sieve is the noun that names the tool.
items.exampleCN: sieve 是给这个工具命名的名词。

items.example: Sift through is the common phrasal use.
items.exampleCN: sift through 是常见短语用法。

items.example: Sift out carries the sense of removing.
items.exampleCN: sift out 带有「去掉」的意思。

items.example: Screen shares the picture of a mesh.
items.exampleCN: screen 共享「网面」的画面。

definition_zh: 路标；指示牌；迹象；路标式提示
definition_en: a post at a road junction that carries signs showing directions and distances, or any clear indication that helps people understand what is happening and what comes next
core_image: 三岔路口竖着一根木桩，木牌上的箭头分别指向不同的城镇
scene: 第一次去那个小镇，我们在岔路口停下来看路标上的公里数。At the fork we stopped to read the signpost before choosing a road.
sceneCN: 这里 signpost 是「路标」（第 1 个义项：立在路口指示方向的牌子）；句意：在岔路口，我们停下来看了看路标，然后才选了一条路。

pos.zh: 在……设置路标；明确标示；提醒

collocations.zh: 通往……的路标；指向……的迹象

derivatives.zh: 由 signpost 加 -ed 构成，指「设有路标的；标示清楚的」
由 signpost 加 -ing 构成，指「路标系统；指引标识」
sign 与 board 组合的近义合成词，义为「招牌；告示牌」

senses.title: A post showing the way on a road
senses.definition: a post beside a road or path with one or more boards that name places and give directions or distances
senses.definitionCN: 立在道路或小路旁、装有一块或多块指示牌的柱子，牌上写地名并给出方向和距离
senses.example: The signpost at the corner pointed right for the castle.
senses.exampleCN: 拐角处的路标指向右边去城堡。
senses.why: The word is a plain compound of sign and post, a visible marker placed to keep walkers and drivers on the right road.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 sign（标志）和 post（柱子）直接组合而成，就是立在路上、帮行人和司机认路的可见标记。

senses.title: A board that names a place or facility
senses.definition: a small board with a name, a number, or an arrow that marks a building, a room, or a service
senses.definitionCN: 写有名称、编号或箭头的小牌子，用来标出建筑、房间或服务设施
senses.example: A wooden signpost marks the start of the trail.
senses.exampleCN: 一块木制标识牌标志着步道的起点。
senses.why: From the junction where several roads meet, the same kind of board is used anywhere people need to be pointed to a place.
senses.whyCN: 路标原本立在多条道路交汇处，同样的牌子也就被用在任何需要给人指明去处的地方。

senses.title: A clear indication of what is coming
senses.definition: something that clearly shows the direction a situation is taking or what is likely to happen next
senses.definitionCN: 清楚显示情势走向或接下来可能发生之事的信号
senses.example: Rising prices are a signpost to a harder year ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 物价上涨是来年更艰难的一个迹象。
senses.why: A signpost tells you which way the road goes, and an indication tells you which way events are going.
senses.whyCN: 路标告诉你路往哪个方向走，而迹象则告诉你事情的走向，比喻的结构完全一样。

senses.title: A passage in a text that shows where to look
senses.definition: a word or short phrase that guides a reader to the next point in a book, a report, or a talk
senses.definitionCN: 引导读者或听众注意下一点的词语或简短语句
senses.example: The examiner looks for signposts such as however and in contrast.
senses.exampleCN: 考官会寻找 however、in contrast 这类引导性的过渡语。
senses.why: The signpost in speech and writing is not on a road but in a line of text, still showing the reader which way to turn.
senses.whyCN: 口语和文章里的路标不在马路上，而在文字行间，起的作用仍然是告诉读者在哪里转弯。

senses.title: To mark a road with signs
senses.definition: to put signs along a road or a route so that people can find the way
senses.definitionCN: 沿道路或路线设置标志，让人能够找到路
senses.example: The council signposted the new cycle route last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 市政厅去年夏天为新自行车道设置了路标。
senses.why: The verb turns the object into an action: to signpost a route is to put the posts there yourself.
senses.whyCN: 动词用法把那个实物变成了动作：signpost 一条路线，就是亲手把这些柱子立上去。

senses.title: To indicate clearly in advance
senses.definition: to show clearly what will happen or how something is to be understood
senses.definitionCN: 清楚地表明将要发生的事或某事应当如何理解
senses.example: The report signposts several risks that need watching.
senses.exampleCN: 报告明确提示了几个需要留意的风险。
senses.why: When a report points to risks, it acts like a road sign instead of a post made of wood.
senses.whyCN: 报告指出风险时，它就在扮演路标的角色，只是那根柱子并不真是木头做的。

intro.en: Signpost is a native English compound of sign, borrowed from Latin signum meaning mark or token, and post, from Latin postis meaning a doorpost or pillar.
intro.cn: signpost 是英语本族复合词，由 sign（源自拉丁语 signum，意为标记）和 post（源自拉丁语 postis，意为门柱、立柱）组合而成。

items.en: Signum means a mark, a token, or a standard, and postis means a post or doorpost.
items.cn: signum 意为标记、记号或旗标，postis 意为柱子或门柱。

items.en: Signe passes into French and then into English as sign.
items.cn: signe 经由法语传入英语，成为 sign。

items.en: The two words are joined as signpost for a roadside marker at a junction.
items.cn: 两个词组合成 signpost，指路口的路标。

items.en: Railway and road designers adopt signpost as a verb for marking routes.
items.cn: 十九世纪铁路与公路设计者开始把 signpost 用作动词，表示给路线设置标志。

items.en: In writing and policy, signpost becomes a metaphor for guidance and clear indication.
items.cn: 在现代写作与政策文本中，signpost 引申为「指引、明确提示」的比喻说法。

note.en: Signpost joins the family of sign words and sits close to the general terms for direction and marking.
note.cn: signpost 属于 sign 一词族，与表示方向、标记的常用词关系很近。

entries.definition: the system of signs on a route
entries.definitionCN: 由 signpost 加 -ing 构成的派生词，义为「路标系统；指引标识」

entries.definition: marked with signs
entries.definitionCN: 由 signpost 加 -ed 构成的派生词，义为「设有路标的」

entries.definition: a board carrying a notice or an advertisement
entries.definitionCN: 由 sign 与 board 组合的合成词，义为「招牌；告示牌」

entries.definition: a post that guides travellers
entries.definitionCN: 指引行人的立柱，与 signpost 几乎同义

entries.definition: an object that shows a position or a boundary
entries.definitionCN: 标记物；界标，强调位置

entries.definition: something that shows a level or a trend
entries.definitionCN: 指示物；指标，强调显示程度

normalIntro.en: Signpost is easy to keep because it is built from two everyday words, a sign on a post standing where roads divide.
normalIntro.cn: signpost 很好记，因为它由两个日常词组成：立在道路分岔处的柱子上的标志。

normal.en: A signpost is literally a sign on a post.
normal.cn: signpost 字面就是「柱子上的标志」。

normal.en: At a fork in the road, read the signpost before you choose.
normal.cn: 在岔路口，先看路标再选路。

normal.en: A signpost to trouble is a warning about what is coming.
normal.cn: signpost to trouble 就是对即将到来之事的预警。

normal.en: When you signpost an essay, you tell the reader where you are going.
normal.cn: 给文章 signpost，就是告诉读者你接下来要讲什么。

normal.en: Compare sign and post: sign gives the mark, post gives the height and the place.
normal.cn: 对比 sign 与 post：前者提供记号，后者提供高度和位置。

abstract.en: Picture a fork in the road with three arrows on one wooden post.
abstract.cn: 想象一根木桩上钉着三个箭头，立在岔路口。

abstract.en: Imagine a shop door with a small board naming the room behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象商店门口一块小牌子，标明门后的房间。

abstract.en: Think of a speaker pausing to say first, then, finally.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者停顿一下，说出「首先、然后、最后」。

examples.en: The signpost showed that the village was two miles ahead.
examples.cn: 路标显示村子还在两英里外。

examples.en: Falling enrolment is a signpost to hard times for the college.
examples.cn: 入学人数下降是学院将面临艰难时期的迹象。

examples.en: All the walking routes are clearly signposted.
examples.cn: 所有步行路线都设有清楚的标识。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赛因坡斯特」——路口竖起的柱子，帮你认路就是 signpost；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: sign（标志，源自拉丁语 signum「标记」）+ post（柱子，源自拉丁语 postis「门柱」）→ signpost（路口立柱上的指路牌）→ 引申为「迹象、指示、明确提示」。

sensesIntro.en: Signpost begins with the roadside sign at a junction, moves to boards naming places, then to signs in the abstract as indications, markers in a text, and finally the verb uses.
sensesIntro.cn: signpost 从路口的路标出发，先指标出场所的牌子，再引申为抽象的迹象、文中的引导提示，最后是动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden post at a fork with arrows pointing to different towns.
core.cn: 核心意象：岔路口一根木桩上钉着箭头，分别指向不同的城镇。

branches.en: The roadside post is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 路边的指路柱是字面义项。

branches.en: Naming a place or facility uses the same board.
branches.cn: 标明场所或设施用的是同一类牌子。

branches.en: An indication points to what events will do, as a sign points to a road.
branches.cn: 迹象指出事情将往哪走，正如路标指出道路通向哪里。

branches.en: The verb is the act of putting signs up or pointing things out clearly.
branches.cn: 动词义就是你亲手立起标志或把事清楚指出的动作。

branches.en: Both the road sign and the linking word keep a reader on the right path.
branches.cn: 路边路标与文章过渡词都让读者走在正确的路上。

intro.en: Signpost combines the Latin borrowing sign with the native and Latin-derived post, and its family grows through the suffixes -ed and -ing.
intro.cn: signpost 把拉丁来源的 sign 与来源兼顾的 post 组合在一起，并通过 -ed、-ing 词尾扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum gives the mark, and Latin postis gives the pillar, so the compound carries both halves of its picture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 signum 提供「标记」，拉丁语 postis 提供「立柱」，这个合成词的两半都有来处。

items.example: Sign names the mark on the board.
items.exampleCN: sign 指牌子上的记号。

items.meaning: a tall upright piece of wood
items.example: Post is the height that holds the board.
items.exampleCN: post 是托住木牌的那根柱子。

items.meaning: a roadside sign showing the way
items.example: Signpost is the full compound.
items.exampleCN: signpost 是完整的合成词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms signposted.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 signposted。

items.example: Signposted describes a marked route.
items.exampleCN: signposted 形容路线设有标识。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或体系的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms signposting.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 signposting。

items.example: Signposting names the whole system.
items.exampleCN: signposting 指整套标识系统。

items.example: Signboard swaps post for board.
items.exampleCN: signboard 把 post 换成了 board。

items.example: Guidepost keeps the same shape.
items.exampleCN: guidepost 保留了同样的结构。

definition_zh: 二氧化硅；硅石；硅胶
definition_en: a white or colourless compound of silicon and oxygen, found in sand, quartz, and many rocks and used to make glass and to dry or absorb things
core_image: 阳光下的一片沙粒，每一颗都是透明的硅氧小晶体
scene: 实验室的干燥器里装着一袋白色颗粒，专门用来吸潮。In the lab, a packet of silica keeps the samples dry.
sceneCN: 这里 silica 是「二氧化硅」（第 1 个义项：沙子、石英的主要成分）；句意：实验室里一小包二氧化硅让样品保持干燥。

derivatives.zh: 由 silic- 词干加 -ate 构成，指「硅酸盐；硅酸酯」
由 silica 加 -eous 构成，指「含硅的；富硅的」
与 silica 同出于拉丁语 silex 的元素名，义为「硅」

senses.title: The compound in sand and quartz
senses.definition: silicon dioxide, the hard white or colourless compound that forms sand, quartz, and much of the earth crust
senses.definitionCN: 二氧化硅，构成沙子、石英和大部分地壳的坚硬白色或无色化合物
senses.example: Sand is mostly made of tiny grains of silica.
senses.exampleCN: 沙子主要由细小的二氧化硅颗粒组成。
senses.why: The name is a modern chemical label built on the Latin word for flint, and it names the substance itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字是以拉丁语「燧石」为词干造出的现代化学名称，直接指称既有物质本身，所以是核心义项。

senses.title: The compound as a material for building and industry
senses.definition: silica used in bulk as a raw material for glass, ceramics, concrete, and other products
senses.definitionCN: 以大宗形式用作玻璃、陶瓷、混凝土等产品原料的二氧化硅
senses.example: Glass manufacturers buy high-grade silica from the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃厂从沙漠地区采购高品位硅石。
senses.why: Once the substance is mined and sold, the same word names it as a commodity.
senses.whyCN: 这种物质一旦被开采、买卖，同一个词就从化学成分变成了商品名称。

senses.title: Granular silica used to absorb moisture
senses.definition: small beads or grains of silica gel that take in water and keep a space dry
senses.definitionCN: 能吸收水分、使周围保持干燥的小颗粒或小珠状硅胶
senses.example: Put a bag of silica inside the box to protect the camera.
senses.exampleCN: 在盒子里放一袋硅胶，保护相机。
senses.why: The chemical has enormous inner surface, so the same substance becomes the little drying packet that follows goods around.
senses.whyCN: 二氧化硅内部表面积极大，同一物质因此变成了跟着货物到处走的那个小干燥剂包。

senses.title: Fine particles that harm the lungs
senses.definition: tiny airborne crystals of silica produced by cutting or grinding stone, which can cause serious lung disease
senses.definitionCN: 切割或打磨石头时产生的、悬浮在空气中的二氧化硅微晶，可引发严重肺病
senses.example: Builders must wear masks to avoid breathing silica.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑工人必须戴口罩，以免吸入硅尘。
senses.why: A material that is harmless as a rock becomes a hazard when it is ground into dust, and the word follows the particles.
senses.whyCN: 石头状态的二氧化硅并无危害，一旦被磨成粉末就变成危险物，这个词也跟着指那些微小颗粒。

senses.title: The compound in soils, plants, and water
senses.definition: silica dissolved or suspended in soil, water, and living things as a nutrient or a trace element
senses.definitionCN: 以养分或微量元素形式溶解或悬浮在土壤、水和生物体内的二氧化硅
senses.example: Some grasses take up silica from the soil to stiffen their stems.
senses.exampleCN: 一些禾草从土壤中吸收硅，使茎秆更硬挺。
senses.why: Ecologists follow the same compound through soil, water, and living tissue, so the label moves with it.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家追着同一种化合物在土壤、水和活体组织间流动，标签也就跟着环境一起移动。

intro.en: Silica is a scientific Latin coinage from silex, the Latin word for flint or hard stone, with the suffix -ica marking a substance.
intro.cn: silica 是科学拉丁语新造词，以 silex（燧石、坚硬石头）为词干，加上表示物质的词尾 -ica 构成。

items.en: Silex means flint or hard stone, the material that gives sparks.
items.cn: silex 意为燧石或坚硬的石头，就是打火时迸出火花的那种石头。

items.en: Chemists form silicium and related terms from the same stem.
items.cn: 十七世纪化学家以同一词干造出 silicium 等相关术语。

items.en: Silica is coined for silicon dioxide as the science of minerals develops.
items.cn: 十九世纪初矿物学发展起来时，为二氧化硅造出 silica 一名。

items.en: English scientific writing borrows silica and uses it for silica in sand and glass.
items.cn: 英语科学文献借入 silica，用于指沙和玻璃中的二氧化硅。

items.en: The twentieth century adds silica gel and warnings about silica dust.
items.cn: 二十世纪又增加了硅胶与硅尘危害的说法。

note.en: Silica shares its Latin flint root with silicon and silicate, and its near meanings are the other mineral and glass words.
note.cn: silica 与 silicon、silicate 共享拉丁语「燧石」词根，近义方面则与矿物和玻璃类词汇相邻。

entries.definition: the chemical element with the symbol Si
entries.definitionCN: 同源于拉丁语 silex 的元素名，义为「硅」，是二氧化硅中的元素

entries.definition: a compound of silicon with oxygen and a metal
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的派生词，义为「硅酸盐」

entries.definition: containing silica
entries.definitionCN: 由 silica 派生的形容词，义为「含硅的」

entries.definition: a hard mineral that is a crystalline form of silica
entries.definitionCN: 近义语境词，指石英，是结晶形态的二氧化硅

entries.definition: loose grains of broken rock, much of it silica
entries.definitionCN: 指沙子，大部分由二氧化硅颗粒组成

entries.definition: a very hard stone that sparks
entries.definitionCN: 指燧石，正是拉丁语 silex 所指的石头

normalIntro.en: Silica is the science word for the stuff of sand: the fleece of microscopic crystals that the Latin word for flint gave its name to.
normalIntro.cn: silica 就是沙子那种东西的科学名称：以拉丁语「燧石」命名的微小晶粒。

normal.en: Silica comes from silex, the Latin word for flint.
normal.cn: silica 来自拉丁语 silex，意思是燧石。

normal.en: Silicon is the element, silica is the compound with oxygen.
normal.cn: silicon 是元素，silica 是与氧结合的化合物。

normal.en: Silica gel is the little packet that keeps shoes dry.
normal.cn: silica gel 就是让鞋子保持干燥的那小包硅胶。

normal.en: Glass and concrete both begin with silica.
normal.cn: 玻璃和混凝土都以二氧化硅为起点。

normal.en: Cutting stone without a mask sends silica into the lungs.
normal.cn: 不戴口罩打磨石头，会让硅尘进入肺部。

abstract.en: Picture a beach where every grain is a tiny clear crystal.
abstract.cn: 想象一片沙滩，每一粒沙都是一颗透明的小晶体。

abstract.en: Imagine a factory melting white sand into clear glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一家工厂把白沙熔成透明玻璃。

abstract.en: Think of a new pair of shoes with a tiny paper packet inside.
abstract.cn: 想一想新鞋盒里那包小小的干燥剂。

examples.en: The desert sand is almost pure silica.
examples.cn: 沙漠里的沙几乎是纯二氧化硅。

examples.en: A sachet of silica gel was hidden under the lid.
examples.cn: 盖子下面藏着一小包硅胶。

examples.en: Workers who cut tiles are exposed to silica dust.
examples.cn: 切割瓷砖的工人会接触到硅尘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「细泥卡」——细小的泥沙结成颗粒，正是二氧化硅；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 silex（燧石、砾石）→ 科学拉丁语 silica（二氧化硅）→ 英语 silica；同词根还生出 silicon（硅）、silicate（硅酸盐），核心义「坚硬的石质化合物」。

sensesIntro.en: Silica starts as the chemical name for silicon dioxide, then names the raw material, the drying gel, the harmful dust, and the dissolved nutrient in soil and water.
sensesIntro.cn: silica 先作二氧化硅的化学名称，再指工业原料、干燥用硅胶、有害硅尘，以及水土中溶解的硅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: each grain of white sand is a tiny clear crystal of silicon and oxygen.
core.cn: 核心意象：每一粒白沙都是一颗硅与氧组成的透明小晶体。

branches.en: The chemical compound in sand is the core sense.
branches.cn: 沙中那种化合物是核心义项。

branches.en: The same compound mined and sold becomes the raw material sense.
branches.cn: 同一种化合物被开采出售后成为原料义项。

branches.en: Absorbing moisture grows out of the huge inner surface of the compound.
branches.cn: 吸湿的功能来自这种化合物巨大的内部表面。

branches.en: Ground to powder, the harmless compound turns into hazardous dust.
branches.cn: 无危害的化合物被磨成粉末后就成了有害的硅尘。

branches.en: Industry and the ecosystem both move silica through soil, water, and products.
branches.cn: 工业与生态系统都让硅在土壤、水和产品之间流动。

intro.en: Silica is built on the Latin stem silic- from silex, with the ending -a typical of substance names, and it grows into silicon, silicate, and siliceous.
intro.cn: silica 建在源自 silex 的拉丁词干 silic- 上，词尾 -a 常见于物质名称，并派生出 silicon、silicate、siliceous。

latinIntro.en: Latin silex means flint, siliceus means flinty, and scientific Latin reuses the stem for silica and silicium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 silex 意为燧石，siliceus 意为多燧石的，科学拉丁语再用这个词干造出 silica 与 silicium。

items.example: Silex is the root noun behind all the silica words.
items.exampleCN: silex 是所有 silica 系词背后的词根名词。

items.example: The stem silic- appears in every derived form.
items.exampleCN: 词干 silic- 出现在每一个派生形式里。

items.example: The ending -a marks silica as a substance in scientific Latin.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -a 使 silica 在科学拉丁语中成为物质名。

items.example: Silica names the compound.
items.exampleCN: silica 指这种化合物。

items.meaningCN: 现代化学中构成元素名的词尾
items.example: Carbon and boron share the element ending.
items.exampleCN: carbon 与 boron 都带元素词尾。

items.example: Silicon is the element inside silica.
items.exampleCN: silicon 是 silica 中的元素。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms silicate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 silicate。

items.meaning: a silicon salt, as in rock
items.example: Most rocks are silicates.
items.exampleCN: 大多数岩石是硅酸盐。

items.meaningCN: 表示具有某种性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -eous forms siliceous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -eous 构成 siliceous。

items.example: Siliceous rocks are rich in silica.
items.exampleCN: siliceous 形容岩石富含硅。

definition_zh: 硅；硅元素；芯片里的硅材料
definition_en: a very common chemical element found in sand and rock, whose pure forms are used in glass, in computer chips and in solar cells
core_image: 海滩上的沙子被熔成透明的玻璃，又被切成一片片亮闪闪的芯片
scene: 实验室里，研究员把一片薄薄的圆片举到灯光下，上面刻满了密密麻麻的小线路。The engineer held up a wafer of silicon covered with tiny circuits.
sceneCN: 这里 silicon 是「芯片里的硅材料」（第 3 个义项：用作电子器件的硅片）；句意为工程师举起一片布满微小电路的硅晶圆。

pos.zh: 硅（化学元素）；硅材料；硅片
（构成复合词）硅制的，如硅芯片

collocations.zh: 硅谷（高科技产业聚集地）

forms.label: 复数（作名词时，一般不用复数）

derivatives.zh: 由硅加拉丁后缀 -a 构成，指二氧化硅
silicon 加由拉丁语 -atus 演变来的后缀，指硅酸盐
由 silica 加形容词后缀 -eous 构成，指含硅的
silicon 加上化学家约定的 -one 词尾，指硅酮
由 silicon 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，指给钢材渗硅

senses.title: The chemical element of atomic number fourteen
senses.definition: a greyish, hard, brittle non-metal element that is the second most abundant element in the crust of the earth
senses.definitionCN: 一种灰硬而脆的非金属元素，占地壳元素含量的第二位
senses.example: Sand consists mainly of compounds of silicon and oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 沙子主要由硅与氧的化合物组成。
senses.why: The mineralogist Davy named the new element silicon, a Latin-looking form built on silica, when he proposed it in eighteen eight; it names the element at the very centre of quartz, flint and sand.
senses.whyCN: 矿物学家戴维在提出该元素时，以二氧化硅的拉丁名词为底，造出拉丁化的 silicon 来指元素；它正是石英、燧石和沙子的中心成分。

senses.title: The element as a technical material
senses.definition: the element used in industry, especially in the form of pure silicon or its compounds such as glass and alloy additives
senses.definitionCN: 工业上使用的该元素，尤指纯硅或其化合物，如玻璃与合金添加剂
senses.example: Glass is widely described as a silicon-based material.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃常被称为硅基材料。
senses.why: Because the element forms glass, cement and strong alloys, industry began to name the material itself silicon, not only the abstract element.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个元素能造出玻璃、水泥和坚固合金，工业界开始用 silicon 指这种材料本身，而不只是抽象的元素。

senses.title: The material of computer chips
senses.definition: the purified material of a wafer from which computer chips and solar cells are made, and by extension the chip industry itself
senses.definitionCN: 用来制作计算机芯片和太阳能电池的纯化晶圆材料，并引申指芯片产业
senses.example: Most of the world market for silicon chips lies in Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 全球大部分硅芯片市场位于亚洲。
senses.why: From the nineteen seventies the purified element became the substrate of microchips, so silicon came to stand for the information age and for the industry built around it.
senses.whyCN: 自 20 世纪七十年代起，纯硅成为微芯片的基底材料，于是 silicon 被用来代表信息时代以及围绕它建立的产业。

senses.title: Silicon with a capital S, the place name
senses.definition: a shortened way of naming a high-technology region modelled on the original one in California
senses.definitionCN: 仿照加州原产地而命名的高科技产业区，如「硅谷」「硅林」
senses.example: The press calls the new software district a second Silicon Valley.
senses.exampleCN: 媒体把新的软件园区称作第二个硅谷。
senses.why: The nickname of one valley in California, coined from the element in its chips, became a model that other regions copied with their own first part, such as forests or beaches.
senses.whyCN: 加州一处山谷因盛产芯片而得到昵称，这个模式被其他地区沿用，只更换前面的地点意象，比如森林或海滩。

senses.title: In chemistry, the symbol Si
senses.definition: the short sign by which the element is written in a formula or on the periodic table
senses.definitionCN: 化学式与元素周期表中书写该元素的简称
senses.example: The formula reads SiO2 for the main constituent of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 沙子主要成分的化学式写作 SiO2。
senses.why: Like every element, silicon is given a one- or two-letter sign taken from its Latin-based name, so the sign Si travels into every formula.
senses.whyCN: 和所有元素一样，硅用取自其拉丁化词名的字母作符号，于是符号 Si 出现在每一个化学式里。

intro.en: Silicon is a modern scientific coinage, built in the early eighteen hundreds on the Latin word for flint, and it later gave its name to glass, plastics and whole industries.
intro.cn: silicon 是近代科学造出的词，在十九世纪初以拉丁语中表示「燧石」的名词为底，后来又把名字给了玻璃、塑料和整片产业。

items.en: Latin silex, genitive silicis, meant hard stone, especially flint.
items.cn: 拉丁语 silex（属格 silicis）指坚硬的石头，尤指燧石。

items.en: Early chemists used a Latin-style noun silica for the earthy substance they got from flint.
items.cn: 早期化学家以拉丁化名词 silica 指从燧石中得到的粉状物质。

items.en: Humphry Davy proposed silicon as the name of the new element, as if it were a Latin noun made from silica.
items.cn: 汉弗莱·戴维提议用 silicon 作新元素的名称，形式上像是从 silica 变出的拉丁语名词。

items.en: Berzelius and others obtained elemental silicon, and the name settled into use.
items.cn: 贝采利乌斯等人制得单质硅，这个名字随之确定下来。

items.en: The chemist Woehler proposed silicone for the carbon-like compounds now used in sealants and cookware.
items.cn: 化学家维勒提出 silicone，指一类类似碳化合物的物质，如今用于密封胶和厨具。

items.en: The nickname Silicon Valley, coined earlier for a district in California, spread worldwide as a model for technology regions.
items.cn: 更早造出的地名硅谷先指加州一处街区，后在世界各地推广，成为科技园区的样板。

note.en: Silicon looks close to its twin silicone and to the mineral words built on the same stem, while its near meanings belong to the world of sand, minerals and chips.
note.cn: silicon 与形近的 silicone 以及同词干长出的矿物词很像，而它的近义词则来自沙、矿物与芯片的世界。

entries.definition: a soft rubbery artificial compound of silicon and oxygen with organic groups
entries.definitionCN: 硅氧与有机基团形成的软橡胶状人造化合物；与 silicon 只差一个字母，但一为元素、一为化合物

entries.definition: silicon dioxide, the white or glassy substance found in quartz and sand
entries.definitionCN: 二氧化硅，石英与沙中的白色或玻璃状物质，是同词干的矿物名

entries.definition: a compound of silicon, oxygen and a metal, forming most of the rocks of the earth
entries.definitionCN: 硅、氧与金属组成的化合物，构成地壳岩石的大部分

entries.definition: a small piece of silicon carrying an integrated circuit
entries.definitionCN: 载有集成电路的小片硅；日常口语中常用来代替 silicon 指硬件

entries.definition: made with silicon as the main element
entries.definitionCN: 以硅为主要成分的，如硅基材料与硅基生命设想

entries.definition: a material that conducts electricity only partly, as silicon does
entries.definitionCN: 导电性介于导体与绝缘体之间的材料，硅即典型半导体

normalIntro.en: Silicon is a Latin-made name for the stuff of flint, and its compounds stand in a row: silica, silicate, silicon, silicone.
normalIntro.cn: silicon 是用拉丁语材料为「燧石之物」造出的名字，它的同族词排成一行：silica、silicate、silicon、silicone。

normal.en: The stem silic- comes from Latin silex, flint, so every word in this family points back to hard stone.
normal.cn: 词干 silic- 来自拉丁语 silex（燧石），这族词里的每一个都指回坚硬的石头。

normal.en: Silica is the dioxide, silicate the salt, silicon the element, and silicone the rubbery compound: one stem, four stages.
normal.cn: silica 是二氧化物，silicate 是盐，silicon 是元素，silicone 是橡胶状化合物：一个词干，四个台阶。

normal.en: Note the final -e in silicone: that extra letter marks the plastic-like material used in baking mats.
normal.cn: 注意 silicone 结尾的 -e：这个多出的字母标记着用于烤垫的那种类塑料材料。

normal.en: Silicon has no plural in ordinary use, and one says pieces of silicon rather than silicons.
normal.cn: silicon 在日常用法里没有复数，说 pieces of silicon，而不说 silicons。

normal.en: Compare carbon: carbon builds life, silicon builds rock, glass and circuits, so chemists call the two cousins.
normal.cn: 对比 carbon：碳构建生命，硅构建岩石、玻璃与电路，化学家把两者称作表亲。

abstract.en: Picture a handful of ordinary beach sand, and remember that this grey powder is the element.
abstract.cn: 想象抓一把普通的海滩细沙，记住这捧灰色粉末就是硅元素。

abstract.en: Imagine a sand grain heated until it flows clear as glass over a window frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒沙被烧到流动清亮，然后铺在窗框上成了玻璃。

abstract.en: See the same grain cut into a thin wafer and printed with a maze of silver lines.
abstract.cn: 再看同样的沙粒被切成薄片，印上银色的迷宫线路。

examples.en: Silicon is the second most abundant element in the crust.
examples.cn: 硅是地壳中含量第二丰富的元素。

examples.en: The plant turns quartz into silicon for solar panels.
examples.cn: 这家工厂把石英加工成太阳能板用的硅。

examples.en: Cheap processing made the silicon chip the heart of modern electronics.
examples.cn: 廉价的加工技术让硅芯片成为现代电子产品的核心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西历孔」——西方的历法刻在硅制的镜片上；这只是谐音拆法，与词源无关，真实来源是拉丁语的燧石。

root: 拉丁语 silex（属格 silicis，燧石、硬石）→ 近代拉丁 silica（硅石）→ 英语 silicon（硅元素）→ 硅片 → 硅谷。核心是「燧石里的物质」。

sensesIntro.en: Silicon begins as the name of an element, spreads to the industrial material, then to the wafer inside a chip, and at last to the industry and even the districts named after it.
sensesIntro.cn: silicon 先是元素的名称，再扩展到工业材料，接着指芯片里的硅片，最后指整个产业乃至以它命名的园区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sand under the feet turned into a sheet of glass and then into a wafer of circuits.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚下的沙先变成一片玻璃，再变成一片布满电路的晶圆。

branches.en: A named element is the sense that chemistry records.
branches.cn: 化学记录的元素名是第一层含义。

branches.en: The industrial material is the sense that factories use.
branches.cn: 工业材料是工厂使用的那层含义。

branches.en: The chip material is where the modern reader meets the word daily.
branches.cn: 芯片材料是现代读者每天都能遇到的那层含义。

branches.en: Place names copying the California district extend the element to geography.
branches.cn: 仿照加州街区得到的地名，把元素含义延伸到地理。

branches.en: The element sense and its chemical sign belong to the same chemistry.
branches.cn: 元素义与化学符号义属于同一套化学语言。

intro.en: Silicon rests on the Latin stem silic-, flint, and the family around it is unusually rich because chemists kept forming new technical nouns from the same stem.
intro.cn: silicon 立在拉丁词干 silic-（燧石）之上，围绕它的同族词格外多，因为化学家不断用同一词干造新的技术名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin silex, genitive silicis, meant flint, and silica became the scholarly Latin noun for the substance found in it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 silex（属格 silicis）意为燧石，silica 后来成为学术拉丁语中指其中物质的名词。

items.example: Silex is the root behind every silic- word.
items.exampleCN: silex 是所有 silic- 词的根。

items.example: Silica was named before the element was isolated.
items.exampleCN: silica 在元素被分离出来之前就已得名。

items.example: Silicon was proposed in eighteen eight.
items.exampleCN: silicon 这个名字在一八零八年被提出。

items.example: The ending -on marks non-metals like carbon and boron.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -on 标记碳、硼这类非金属。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms silicate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 silicate。

items.meaning: a compound of silicon, oxygen and metal
items.example: Silicate makes up most rock.
items.exampleCN: 硅酸盐构成大部分岩石。

items.example: The suffix -eous forms siliceous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -eous 构成 siliceous。

items.example: Siliceous rock is rich in silica.
items.exampleCN: 硅质岩富含二氧化硅。

items.example: Silicone keeps its shape when hot.
items.exampleCN: 硅酮受热仍保持形状。

items.example: The silicon chip changed computing.
items.exampleCN: 硅芯片改变了计算。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 燧石中的土状物质；硅石

definition_zh: 蚕；家蚕；吐丝结茧的幼虫
definition_en: a caterpillar kept in captivity that eats mulberry leaves and spins a white cocoon of silk thread
core_image: 一双苍白的胖毛虫趴在桑叶上，一层层吐出耀眼的白丝把自己裹成茧
scene: 农家竹匾里铺满桑叶，白胖的虫子正把丝一圈圈绕上自己。The children watched a silkworm spin its cocoon in the corner of the tray.
sceneCN: 这里 silkworm 是「家蚕」（第 1 个义项：被人饲养、以桑叶为食的蛾类幼虫）；句意为孩子们看着一条蚕在竹匾角落结茧。

derivatives.zh: silkworm 去掉后部得到的词，指蚕吐出的丝与丝织品
silk 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，指像丝绸般柔滑的
silkworm 与 moth 组合，指蚕蛾，即家蚕的成虫
由丝与筛网合称而来的丝网印刷法，与 silkworm 共享 silk 词干

senses.title: The caterpillar bred for silk
senses.definition: the larva of the domesticated silk moth, raised on mulberry leaves and valued for the cocoon it spins
senses.definitionCN: 家蚕蛾的幼虫，以桑叶饲养，因能结茧而珍贵
senses.example: Silkworms feed on mulberry leaves for weeks before they spin.
senses.exampleCN: 蚕要连吃几周桑叶才开始吐丝。
senses.why: The word joins silk, the thread it makes, with the Old English worm that once meant any crawling creature, so the name says what the animal is for.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「丝」和古英语里泛指爬虫的 worm 拼在一起，名字直接说出了这种动物的用途。

senses.title: The mulberry silk moth, Bombyx mori
senses.definition: the pale moth species itself, known only in domestication and no longer found in the wild
senses.definitionCN: 家蚕蛾这个物种本身，只在人工饲养中存在，野外已无种群
senses.example: The adult silkworm is a stout moth with no urge to fly.
senses.exampleCN: 蚕的成虫是一只笨重的蛾子，几乎不想飞。
senses.why: Because the larva was the only stage people ever saw in the shed, its name simply became the species name, so the word now names the whole insect.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们只在蚕室里看到幼虫这一阶段，幼虫名便顺理成章地成了物种名，于是这个词也指整只昆虫。

senses.title: Silk culture as an activity
senses.definition: the practice, trade or science of raising the insect for its thread
senses.definitionCN: 为取丝而饲养这种昆虫的生产活动、行业或学问
senses.example: Silkworm farming spread westward along the old trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 养蚕业沿古代商路向西传播。
senses.why: When a single animal supports a whole trade, its everyday name easily shifts to name the trade itself, as hen can stand for poultry keeping.
senses.whyCN: 当一种动物支撑起整个行业，它的日常名字很容易转而指这个行业，就像母鸡可以代指养禽业。

senses.title: In metaphor, a person drawn into wearing themselves out
senses.titleCN: 作茧自缚的人；甘愿耗尽自己的人
senses.definition: a person who works so devotedly or self-sacrificingly that the effort consumes them
senses.definitionCN: 过于投入、以至自我消耗的人
senses.example: He works like a silkworm, giving thread until nothing is left.
senses.exampleCN: 他像蚕一样工作，吐丝直到一无所有。
senses.why: The larva spends its body making a thread that is then unwound by others, and that image of unreturned sacrifice became a stock metaphor in both English and Chinese.
senses.whyCN: 幼虫把身体耗在吐出被别人抽走的丝上，这种没有回报的奉献意象在英语与汉语里都成了固定比喻。

intro.en: Silkworm is a plain English compound of silk and worm; the word silk itself arrived along the silk routes from the Greek and Latin names for the thread.
intro.cn: silkworm 是 silk 与 worm 这两个本地词组成的朴素复合词；silk 本身则沿丝路辗转来自希腊语与拉丁语中表示这种丝线的名称。

items.en: Greek serikon named the silk cloth that reached the Mediterranean from the East.
items.cn: 希腊语 serikon 指从东方运到地中海的丝织物。

items.en: Latin sericum carried the same word, and sericus meant silken, whence the modern Latin name of the moth family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sericum 沿用了同一个词，形容词 sericus 意为丝的，现代拉丁语中蚕蛾的科名即由此而来。

items.en: Old English sidolc, of uncertain further origin, names the imported cloth long before the insect itself is recorded.
items.cn: 古英语 sidolc 指这种进口织物，更早的来源不确定；它远在昆虫本身被记录之前就已出现。

items.en: Through Old English seolc and Old Norse silki the medieval form silk became standard.
items.cn: 经古英语 seolc 与古诺斯语 silki，中世纪形式 silk 成为标准写法。

items.en: Old English wyrm meant serpent or crawling creature, and worm later narrowed to the earthworm and the larvae in this word.
items.cn: 古英语 wyrm 指蛇或爬行的生物，后来 worm 的含义缩小到蚯蚓，以及本词中表示的幼虫。

items.en: Silkworm fixed the compound for the mulberry-fed caterpillar, and the first date of the compound is uncertain.
items.cn: silkworm 固化为这位吃桑叶的幼虫的名字；该复合词的首见年代存疑。

note.en: Silkworm is half worm and half silk, so it stands beside its shorter relatives and beside the moths, caterpillars and silk words of the same field.
note.cn: silkworm 一半是 worm、一半是 silk，因此它的近邻既有更短的亲属词，也有同属一个领域的蛾、毛虫与丝制品词。

entries.definition: the fine soft thread spun by the silkworm, and the cloth made from it
entries.definitionCN: 蚕吐出的细软丝线以及用它织成的布，是 silkworm 的前半个词

entries.definition: smooth and soft like silk
entries.definitionCN: 像丝一样光滑柔软的，由 silk 加后缀构成，与蚕丝的光泽同源

entries.definition: the adult moth whose larva is the silkworm
entries.definitionCN: 幼虫即蚕的成虫，也就是蚕蛾

entries.definition: the worm-like larva of a butterfly or moth
entries.definitionCN: 蝴蝶或蛾的毛虫状幼虫；silkworm 正是其中一种被驯养的毛虫

entries.definition: the covering of silk that a larva spins round itself
entries.definitionCN: 幼虫吐丝把自己裹起来的茧，是养蚕的收获所在

entries.definition: the technical name for the breeding of silkworms
entries.definitionCN: 养蚕业的学术名称，字面意为「丝的耕种」

normalIntro.en: Silkworm is a speaking compound: the animal is named after the product, and the same animal has a caterpillar body and a moth body.
normalIntro.cn: silkworm 是「会说话的复合词」：动物以产品命名，而同一只动物先有毛虫的身体，后有蛾子的身体。

normal.en: Silk plus worm: the second element tells you the shape, the first tells you the value.
normal.cn: silk 加 worm：后一个词说明体型，前一个词说明价值。

normal.en: Worm is old English for any crawling creature, so in a compound it often means a larva rather than an earthworm.
normal.cn: worm 在古英语里泛指爬行的生物，所以在复合词里它常指幼虫而不是蚯蚓。

normal.en: Keep silk and silkworm apart: silk is the thread, silkworm is the creature that makes it.
normal.cn: 把 silk 和 silkworm 分开记：silk 是丝，silkworm 是吐丝的虫。

normal.en: The adult is called a silkworm moth, because the larva is the stage that feeds and earns the name.
normal.cn: 成虫叫 silkworm moth，因为只有幼虫大量进食，也正是取名的那个阶段。

normal.en: Notice the false friend in Chinese: the word for silk and the word for silkworm are two different Chinese characters.
normal.cn: 注意这个中文陷阱：silk 是丝，silkworm 是蚕，两者用字不同。

abstract.en: Picture a pale caterpillar eating a mulberry leaf down to its ribs, its body growing fatter by the hour.
abstract.cn: 想象的画面：一只苍白毛虫把一片桑叶啃得只剩叶脉，身体每小时都在变胖。

abstract.en: Imagine a slow white ribbon leaving its mouth and wrapping round its own body in loops.
abstract.cn: 想象的画面：一条白色细带从嘴里缓缓抽出，一圈圈绕在自己的身体上。

abstract.en: See a shed full of trays of wriggling white bodies, every tray tended by hand.
abstract.cn: 想象的画面：装满竹匾的蚕室里，每一匾白胖的身体都在蠕动，全靠双手照料。

examples.en: A silkworm spins a single thread that can be hundreds of metres long.
examples.cn: 一条蚕吐出的丝可以长达数百米。

examples.en: Silkworms were first domesticated in China thousands of years ago.
examples.cn: 蚕在数千年前最先在中国被驯化。

examples.en: The cocoon is unwound and twisted into the finest silk.
examples.cn: 蚕茧被抽成丝，再捻成上等的丝绸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「丝儿捆」——丝儿一圈圈捆成一只虫，就是蚕；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 silk（丝，经古英语 seolc 与古诺斯语 silki 源自希腊语 serikon、拉丁语 sericum 的丝名）+ 古英语 worm（虫，原指一切爬行生物）→ silkworm「吐丝的虫」。核心是「产丝之虫」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with the caterpillar kept for its thread, then names the whole insect, the trade that feeds on it, and finally a person who spreads himself thin.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指被养来取丝的幼虫，再指整只昆虫，接着指靠它兴起的产业，最后指把自己耗干的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white caterpillar turning itself into a single shining thread.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条白色的虫子把自己变成一根闪亮的丝线。

branches.en: The fed caterpillar is the sense the farmer knows.
branches.cn: 被饲养的幼虫是养蚕人最熟悉的那层含义。

branches.en: The moth species is the sense a biologist uses.
branches.cn: 蛾的物种是生物学家使用的含义。

branches.en: The trade is the sense an economist meets.
branches.cn: 产业是经济学家会遇到的义项。

branches.en: The devoted person is the figurative sense quoted from old sayings.
branches.cn: 自我耗尽的奉献者是从旧语中引用来的比喻义。

branches.en: The caterpillar and the trade are two halves of one rural economy in both language and literature.
branches.cn: 幼虫与产业是同一门农村经济的两半，在语言与传统文本里都成双出现。

intro.en: Silkworm is a native compound rather than a Latin construction, and its main piece silk comes with a small family of its own.
intro.cn: silkworm 是本地合成的复合词，而非拉丁语的构造；它的主干 silk 自己带一小族词。

latinIntro.en: The silk part traces back to Greek and Latin names for silk cloth, hence the learnt word sericulture, while the worm part has no Latin relative.
latinIntro.cn: silk 部分可追溯到希腊语与拉丁语中的丝绸名，由此有了学术词 sericulture；worm 部分则没有拉丁亲属。

items.example: Seolc names the imported cloth.
items.exampleCN: seolc 指进口的丝织物。

items.example: Old Norse silki shares the word.
items.exampleCN: 古诺斯语 silki 共享这个词根。

items.example: Silk is the short half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: silk 是复合词较短的那一半。

items.example: Wyrm is the ancestor of worm.
items.exampleCN: wyrm 是 worm 的前身。

items.example: Worm supplies the second half.
items.exampleCN: worm 提供复合词的后半。

items.meaning: the caterpillar of the silk moth
items.example: Silkworm joins the thread to the creature.
items.exampleCN: silkworm 把丝与虫连在一起。

items.example: The suffix -y forms silky.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 silky。

items.example: The fabric feels silky.
items.exampleCN: 这块布摸起来丝滑。

items.example: The silk moth lays eggs once.
items.exampleCN: 蚕蛾只产一次卵。

items.example: The silk trade crossed whole continents.
items.exampleCN: 丝绸贸易曾是横跨大陆的生意。

latinEntries.structure: bombyx, bombycis (f., third declension; also Greek)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 蚕；茧，蚕蛾属的学名即取其词形

definition_zh: 淤泥；粉砂；使淤塞；（泥沙）沉积
definition_en: fine mud or sand carried by moving water and left as soft sediment, or to become blocked with such sediment
core_image: 洪水退去后，弯弯的河底铺着一层光滑细腻的浅褐色软泥
scene: 洪水退去后的清晨，河底铺满一层滑腻细软的浅褐色软泥，脚一踩就陷下去。In the morning the flood left a layer of silt across the whole river bed.
sceneCN: 这里 silt 是「淤泥、粉砂」（第 1 个义项：水流带来的细软沉积物）；句意为洪水退去后，整段河床铺上了一层淤泥。

derivatives.zh: silt 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，指含粉砂的、多淤泥的
由 silt 的动词形式加 -ation 构成，指泥沙淤积的过程
silt 与 stone 复合，指由粉砂固结而成的岩石
silt 加 -free 构成，指不含淤沙的

senses.title: Fine sediment carried by water
senses.definition: fine mud or sandy particles that are held in moving water and settle out as soft sediment
senses.definitionCN: 被流动的水悬带、最终沉下来的细泥或细沙颗粒
senses.example: The river carries silt down to the estuary.
senses.exampleCN: 河水把淤泥一路带到河口。
senses.why: The word names the material itself, the soft fine earth that a river drops wherever its current slows, so the physical picture comes before any use of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指物质本身，即河流在水缓处卸下的细软泥土，所以物质画面先于任何用途。

senses.title: Mud blocking a channel or reservoir
senses.definition: the deposit of sediment that blocks or makes shallow a river, harbour, pipe or reservoir
senses.definitionCN: 堵住河道、港口、管道或水库并使其变浅的沉积物
senses.example: Silt has raised the level of the harbour floor.
senses.exampleCN: 淤积使港底抬高。
senses.why: Once the fine grains stack up, they thin the water above them, so the same material that only dirtied the river now makes it shallow and hard to navigate.
senses.whyCN: 细粒一叠高，上面的水就变浅，同一堆东西于是从弄脏河水变成了让河变浅、难以通航。

senses.title: The body of such earth as a land form
senses.definition: a soil or geological layer made largely of silt particles, or ground built up by it
senses.definitionCN: 主要由粉砂颗粒构成的地层或土壤，或由它堆积成的土地
senses.example: The valley floor is deep, rich silt from annual floods.
senses.exampleCN: 谷底是年年洪水带来的深厚肥沃淤土。
senses.why: The same deposit that blocks one channel builds fertile ground in another place, so silt as a land form names the river gift rather than the river fault.
senses.whyCN: 同样的沉积物堵了这里、却在别处堆出沃土，所以作为土地形态的 silt 指河流的馈赠而非过失。

senses.title: Particles that keep water cloudy
senses.titleCN: 悬浮的细泥颗粒；含沙量
senses.definition: the fine particles suspended in water, measured as sediment load or turbidity
senses.definitionCN: 悬浮水中、使水浑浊的细小颗粒，常以含沙量或浑浊度计量
senses.example: Silt in the water blots out light for the fish below.
senses.exampleCN: 水中的细泥挡住了水下鱼类所需的阳光。
senses.why: Silt is light enough to hang in the water for a long while, and that hanging is what makes a river brown, so the name is also used for the suspension itself.
senses.whyCN: silt 足够轻，能在水里悬很久，正是这种悬浮让河水发褐，所以这个词也用来指悬浮颗粒本身。

senses.title: The verb, to become or make blocked
senses.definition: of a river, drain or pool, to fill slowly with sediment, or to fill one with sediment
senses.definitionCN: 河道、排水沟或水塘慢慢被泥沙填满，或使其被填满
senses.example: The old canal has silted up and no boats pass.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧运河已经淤平，不再有船经过。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb with no change of form, and the little up completes the picture of a channel filling from below until it is full.
senses.whyCN: 名词不改变形式就变成动词，再加一个 up，正好画出河道从底下一点点被填满的画面。

intro.en: Silt is probably a form of the older English noun selt or sylt, a variant of salt, in the sense of salt marsh; early uses name the soft mud of tidal estuaries rather than a mineral sort.
intro.cn: silt 可能来自更早的英语名词 selt 或 sylt，即 salt 的异体，取「盐沼」之义；早期用法指潮汐河口里的软泥，而非某种矿物粒径。

items.en: Old English sealt means salt, the material as well as the salty ground.
items.cn: 古英语 sealt 意为盐，既指盐本身，也指盐地。

items.en: Middle English selt and sylt, chiefly of northern and eastern England, name salt marsh and the mud on it.
items.cn: 中古英语 selt 与 sylt 多见于英格兰北部与东部，指盐沼及其上的泥。

items.en: Silt appears in English texts, first as a name for the fine mud of tidal rivers; the spelling is probably a form of selde or sylt.
items.cn: silt 在英语文本中出现，最早指潮汐河里细软的泥；其拼写很可能是 selde 或 sylt 的变体。

items.en: Engineering and geology turned silt into a technical term for a particle size between sand and clay.
items.cn: 工程与地质学把 silt 变成技术术语，指介于沙与黏土之间的粒径。

items.en: The verb and the compound silt up follow the noun and describe channel blocking.
items.cn: 动词用法与词组 silt up 随名词而来，用来描述河道堵塞。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): whether silt continues selt directly or came in through the name of a coastal county or river mouth is unresolved.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：silt 是直接延续 selt，还是经由某沿海郡县或河口之名传入，学界尚无定论。

note.en: Silt belongs to one family of sediment words, some sharing its shape, others sharing its meaning, and all of them concerned with what water leaves behind.
note.cn: silt 属于同一群「沉积物」词，其中有的与它形近，有的与它义近，都与水留下的东西有关。

entries.definition: the process of becoming blocked with fine sediment
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐被细泥填满的过程，是 silt 作动词的分词形式

entries.definition: full of silt
entries.definitionCN: 含淤泥的、粉砂质的，由 silt 加后缀构成

entries.definition: blocked or filled with silt
entries.definitionCN: 已被淤泥堵塞或填满的，是 silt 的过去式与过去分词

entries.definition: matter that settles to the bottom of a liquid
entries.definitionCN: 沉到液体底部的物质，是涵盖 silt 的更宽类别

entries.definition: thick soft mud or industrial waste deposit
entries.definitionCN: 浓稠柔软的泥浆或工业废泥，比 silt 更稠更脏

entries.definition: soft wet earth
entries.definitionCN: 湿软的泥土，泛指湿土而不分粒径

normalIntro.en: Silt is short, soft and quiet: it is what water carries when it is in no hurry, and what it lays down when the current fails.
normalIntro.cn: silt 短、软、安静：它是水不急时带走的细泥，也是水流一停就放下的东西。

normal.en: The word probably grows out of Old English selt, a form of salt, from the muddy marshland of tidal rivers.
normal.cn: 这个词多半由古英语 selt（salt 的变体）长出来，来自潮汐河口的泥泞盐沼。

normal.en: Silt pairs smoothly with up: silt up means the channel fills and the water slows further.
normal.cn: silt 常与 up 搭配：silt up 表示河道被填满，水于是更慢。

normal.en: The adjective silty adds -y on the model of sandy and muddy, and the rock siltstone is compressed silt.
normal.cn: 形容词 silty 仿照 sandy、muddy 加 -y 而成，而 siltstone 是被压实的粉砂。

normal.en: Silt names a grain size between sand and clay, so it is counted as neither the gravel under your boot nor the sticky pot clay.
normal.cn: silt 指沙与黏土之间的粒径，所以它既不是靴下的砾石，也不是做陶的黏土。

normal.en: Compare mud and sediment: sediment is the general word, mud is the wet heap, silt is the fine fraction that settles last.
normal.cn: 对比 mud 与 sediment：sediment 是总称，mud 是湿泥团，silt 是最后沉下的细粒部分。

abstract.en: Watch the brown river go clear in a glass jar overnight and the silt lying at the bottom like a pale blanket.
abstract.cn: 花一夜时间看一只玻璃罐里的褐色河水变清，淤泥就会像一条浅色毯子落在罐底。

abstract.en: Stand at the mouth of the muddy harbour at low tide, and you stand on silt the river has been dropping for centuries.
abstract.cn: 退潮时站在那浑浊港口的口上，你踩的就是河流几百年来一直卸下的淤泥。

abstract.en: See a thin layer of earth that builds a delta piece by piece until land exists where the sea used to be.
abstract.cn: 看一层薄薄的泥土一点点堆成三角洲，直到原来海面的地方长出了陆地。

examples.en: Each spring, the river spreads a new layer of silt over the fields.
examples.cn: 每年春天，河水都会在田野上铺下一层新的淤泥。

examples.en: The reservoir is silting up faster than the planners expected.
examples.cn: 这座水库淤积的速度超出规划者的预料。

examples.en: Fine silt settles here whenever the current slows.
examples.cn: 水流一变慢，细泥便在此处沉积下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「稀了」——河水稀了、也变清了，因为泥沉到底成了淤泥；只是谐音联想，真实来源一般与 salt 的旧形式有关。

root: 一般认为来自古英语 sealt（盐）→ 中古英语 selt、sylt（盐沼、沼泽泥地）→ 英语 silt（潮汐河中的细泥）→ 粉砂、淤积。核心是「水带来又留下的细泥」。

sensesIntro.en: Silt starts as a name for soft river mud, then for the blocking it causes, then for the ground it builds, for the cloudiness it creates, and finally for the act of filling up.
sensesIntro.cn: silt 先指河中的细软泥，继而指它造成的堵塞，再指它堆积成的土地与水中的浑浊，最后指淤塞的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale layer of fine mud left on a river bed after the water drops.
core.cn: 核心意象：水位退去后，河床上留下一层浅色细泥。

branches.en: The material itself is the core of the word.
branches.cn: 物质本身是这个词的核心。

branches.en: The blocking deposit is what engineers measure.
branches.cn: 造成堵塞的沉积物是工程师要测量的。

branches.en: The built ground is what farmers and geologists see.
branches.cn: 淤积成的土地是农民与地质学家所看到的。

branches.en: The cloudy particles are the same grain seen in suspension.
branches.cn: 水中的浑浊颗粒就是悬浮状态下的同一种细粒。

branches.en: The blocking deposit and the verb come from one picture: a channel slowly filling up.
branches.cn: 堵塞的沉积与动词义出自同一幅画面：河道慢慢被填满。

intro.en: Silt is a very short and quiet English noun, and the most important endings in its family are the adjective -y and the technical -ation.
intro.cn: silt 是极短而安静的英语名词，这一族里最重要的词尾是形容词的 -y 与技术类名词的 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Silt has no reliable Latin relative, so the Latin side stays as the family of the ancient salt word it descends from.
latinIntro.cn: silt 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，所以拉丁语部分只列出它所源自的那个古老盐名一族。

items.example: Selt names the muddy marsh.
items.exampleCN: selt 指泥泞的沼泽。

items.example: Silt settles out when water slows.
items.exampleCN: 水一慢，淤泥就沉下来。

items.example: The harbour silted up within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 港口在十年内就淤塞了。

items.example: The suffix -y forms silty.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 silty。

items.example: Silty ground holds water poorly.
items.exampleCN: 粉砂质的地面保水差。

items.meaningCN: 表示过程或行动的词尾
items.example: The ending -ation forms siltation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 siltation。

items.example: Dams slow flow and speed siltation.
items.exampleCN: 水坝使流速变慢，加快淤积。

items.example: Siltstone layers are soft and fine.
items.exampleCN: 粉砂岩层松软细腻。

items.example: The suffix -free forms silt-free.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -free 构成 silt-free。

items.example: The filter returns silt-free water.
items.exampleCN: 过滤器给出不含淤沙的水。

definition_zh: 相似性；相像之处；类似；相似程度
definition_en: the quality of being alike, or a particular way in which two or more things resemble each other
core_image: 两块并排的石头，花纹几乎一样，只有细看才见差别
scene: 老师把两篇作文并排放在投影上，让全班找出共同点。The teacher asked us to underline every similarity between the two essays.
sceneCN: 这里 similarity 是「相像之处」（第 1 个义项：两件事物共有、可以让它们被放在一起比较的可比点）；句意：老师要求我们在两篇作文之间每一处相似之处下面画线。

pos.zh: 名词：相似性；相像之处；相似程度

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ity 得到的基础形容词，义为「相似的；类似的」
由 similar 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「同样地；类似地」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 similar 构成，义为「不相似的；不同的」
由 dis- 加到本词构成，义为「不相似；差异之处」

senses.title: The quality of being alike
senses.definition: the state or quality of resembling something else, often to a noticeable degree
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相像的状态或性质，通常指相像程度明显
senses.example: There is a strong similarity between the two dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种方言之间有很大相似性。
senses.why: Latin similis meant like or of the same kind, so similarity names the shared likeness itself rather than any one object.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 similis 意为「相像的、同类的」，所以 similarity 指的是那份共同的相像，而不是某一件东西。

senses.title: A particular point in common
senses.definition: a specific feature, detail, or respect in which two or more things are alike
senses.definitionCN: 两个或更多事物相像的某个具体特征、细节或方面
senses.example: The report lists three similarities between the two crashes.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了两次撞车事故的三个共同点。
senses.why: An abstract quality can be counted, so one shared feature becomes one similarity and several become similarities.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的性质可以被计数，于是一个共同特征就是一处 similarity，几个就是 similarities。

senses.title: Measured resemblance
senses.definition: the extent to which things match, as measured in studies, tests, or data analysis
senses.definitionCN: 在实验、测试或数据分析中测得的吻合程度
senses.example: The software rates the similarity of the two texts at ninety per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 软件判定这两段文字有九成相似。
senses.why: Once likeness is a quality, it can be graded; measurement turns the felt resemblance into a number.
senses.whyCN: 相像既然是一种性质，就可以分等级；测量把感觉到的相似变成了具体数值。

senses.title: Similarity in structure or form
senses.definition: resemblance in shape, pattern, or arrangement rather than in function or meaning
senses.definitionCN: 形状、图案或排列上的相似，而非功能或意义上的相似
senses.example: The similarity in body shape helps the two insects hide on the same bark.
senses.exampleCN: 两者体形的相似让这两种昆虫能藏在同一片树皮上。
senses.why: Because the root sense is plain likeness, structure and appearance can be compared even when function differs.
senses.whyCN: 因为本义只是朴素的相像，所以即使功能不同，结构与外观也能被拿来比较。

senses.title: Similarity of tone or style
senses.definition: a likeness in style, voice, or manner that listeners or readers can hear or sense
senses.definitionCN: 听众或读者能够听到或感受到的风格、语气、方式上的相像
senses.example: Readers noted the similarity of tone between the two novels.
senses.exampleCN: 读者注意到这两部小说语气上的相似。
senses.why: Style is a quality of a text, so two texts with the same voice stand in exactly the same relation as two similar stones.
senses.whyCN: 风格是文本的一种性质，两篇声音相同的文本，其关系正如两块相像的石头。

senses.title: Similarity in genetic or family make-up
senses.definition: the degree to which living things or languages share inherited features
senses.definitionCN: 生物或语言之间共享可继承特征的多少
senses.example: Genetic similarity can suggest how closely two species are related.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传上的相似程度可以提示两个物种亲缘关系的远近。
senses.why: Family members resemble one another by inheritance, so likeness drifts from appearance into shared descent.
senses.whyCN: 同一家族的成员因遗传而彼此相像，于是相似从外观延伸到共同的来源。

senses.title: Similarity that is only apparent
senses.definition: a likeness that looks convincing but turns out to hide a genuine difference
senses.definitionCN: 看起来很有说服力、实则掩盖了真实差异的相似
senses.example: Any surface similarity between the two cases soon disappears under a closer look.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细一看，两案之间任何表面上的相似很快就不见了。
senses.why: If likeness can be explained by another cause, the word is used to warn that the match is probably coincidence.
senses.whyCN: 如果相像可以由别的因素解释，这个词就用来提醒：这种吻合很可能是巧合。

intro.en: Similarity is a Latin-derived noun: similis meant like, and the suffix -ity turns that likeness into a nameable quality.
intro.cn: similarity 是由拉丁语而来的名词：similis 意为「相像的」，后缀 -ity 把这份相像变成可以命名的性质。

items.en: Similis meant like or of the same kind. The older root behind it is generally reconstructed, but the exact form is not certain.
items.cn: similis 意为「相像的、同类的」。它更早的词根一般认为可以重构，但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: Latin formed the abstract noun similitudo, a likeness, often through the common suffix -tudo that names a quality.
items.cn: 拉丁语构成抽象名词 similitudo，意为「相似」，多借助表示性质的常用后缀 -tudo。

items.en: A later form similaritas applied the suffix -itas, the ancestor of English -ity, to the same adjective.
items.cn: 较晚的形式 similaritas 把后缀 -itas（英语 -ity 的前身）加到同一个形容词上。

items.en: The noun appears in English in the fifteenth century, and the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词于十五世纪进入英语，确切的首见记录不确定。

items.en: English turns likeness into something that can be counted, graded and computed, giving points in common, degrees and scores.
items.cn: 现代英语把相像变成可以计数、分级和计算的东西，于是有了共同点、相似度和相似分数。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin likeness root; the near-meaning group gathers words for resemblance, identity and sameness that differ in strength.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「相像」的拉丁词根；近义组收表示「像、同为、相同」的一批词，它们在程度上有差别。

entries.definition: Like something else in some way, usually without being exactly the same.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「相似的、类似的」，通常并非完全相同，是相似性的基础形容词。

entries.definition: In a like way, used to link two clauses or sentences.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「同样地、类似地」，用来连接两个分句或句子。

entries.definition: Not alike, with the negative prefix dis- added to the same adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不相似的」，由否定的 dis- 加到同一形容词上。

entries.definition: A likeness between people or things, often slightly more formal and visual than similarity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「相像、相似之处」，比相似性常更正式，也多指外观上的相像。

entries.definition: The state of looking like something, or a picture or copy of a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「相像」或「画像」，英式英语里常指人的肖像。

entries.definition: The quality of being identical, stronger than similarity and often dull.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「相同、千篇一律」，比相似程度更强，常带单调乏味的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root similis and the phrases the noun actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 similis，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: similis is the same root that gives similar, so similarity is simply similar with a noun ending.
normal.cn: similis 是构成 similar 的同一词根，所以 similarity 就是在 similar 后面换个名词词尾。

normal.en: Bear a similarity to means to look like something in some visible way.
normal.cn: bear a similarity to 意为在某方面看起来像某物。

normal.en: A striking similarity is one that is noticed at once; a surface similarity is one that may hide a real difference.
normal.cn: striking similarity 是一眼就能注意到的相似；surface similarity 则可能掩盖真实差异。

normal.en: The father of the family is the abstract noun that names a quality, just as clarity names being clear.
normal.cn: 这一词族的中心是命名一种性质的抽象名词，就像 clarity 命名「清楚」一样。

normal.en: Compare similar and identical: similar things are alike, identical things are exactly the same.
normal.cn: 对比 similar 与 identical：相似的事物只是相像，相同的事物则完全一样。

abstract.en: Picture two stones side by side, their patterns almost the same, and one tiny crack as the only difference.
abstract.cn: 想象两块石头并排放着，花纹几乎一样，只有一道细缝是唯一的差别。

abstract.en: Imagine a teacher holding two essays up to the light and circling the phrases that match.
abstract.cn: 想象老师把两篇作文举到光下，把吻合的词句圈出来。

abstract.en: Think of a ruler laid across two similar outlines to show how close the match is.
abstract.cn: 想象用一把尺子横在两条相似的轮廓上，量出它们有多接近。

examples.en: Scientists were surprised by the similarity between the two sets of fossils.
examples.cn: 科学家对这两组化石之间的相似性感到惊讶。

examples.en: Despite some similarities, the two systems run very differently.
examples.cn: 尽管有一些相似之处，这两个系统的运行方式差异很大。

examples.en: The court looked at the similarity of the two trademarks before ruling.
examples.cn: 法院在裁决前考察了这两个商标的相似程度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「相似啦」——两块石头摆在一起，怎么看都像：相似性。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 similis（相像的、同类的）→ 抽象名词 similitudo → 晚期拉丁语 similaritas（加后缀 -itas，即英语 -ity 的前身）→ 英语 similarity，核心义「共有可比的相像」。同根词有 similar、assimilate、simulate（后两个经前缀与词干变化而来）。

sensesIntro.en: Similarity starts from a plain quality of being alike, then grows into countable points in common, measured degrees, and likeness in form, style, descent, or mere appearance.
sensesIntro.cn: similarity 从「相像」这一朴素性质出发，扩展为可数的共同点、可测量的相似度，以及结构、风格、亲缘甚至表面上的相像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two stones side by side with almost the same pattern and one tiny crack.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块并排的石头，花纹几乎一样，只差一道细缝。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: the abstract name for being alike, the noun that sits at the head of the family.
branches.cn: 性质线：表示「相像」的抽象名词，位于这一词族的中心。

branches.en: THE COUNT: once likeness is a quality, each shared feature can be counted separately.
branches.cn: 计数线：相像既然是一种性质，每一处共同特征就能单独计数。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: tests and data analysis turn the quality into a score or percentage.
branches.cn: 数值线：测试与数据分析把这份性质变成分数或百分比。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: shape, pattern and style are likenesses you can see or hear without knowing meaning.
branches.cn: 表面线：形状、图案与风格是无需理解意义就能看见或听见的相像。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: shared descent explains real likeness, while similarity with no good cause warns of a coincidence.
branches.cn: 成因线：共同来源解释真实的相像，而不明原因的相似则提醒人们那可能只是巧合。

intro.en: Similarity is built from a Latin adjective of likeness plus a very common abstract noun suffix.
intro.cn: similarity 由表示「相像」的拉丁语形容词加上一个十分常见的抽象名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis and similitudo are both recorded, and the suffix here is the Latin -itas, which English reshaped as -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 similis 与 similitudo 均有文献记录，本词所用后缀即拉丁语 -itas，英语把它改写成 -ity。

items.example: The adjective is the likeness root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是这一词族表示「相像」的词根。

items.example: The suffix -tudo names a quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tudo 用来命名一种性质。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成抽象名词。

items.example: The adjective is the everyday form.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是日常使用的形式。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms similarity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 similarity。

items.example: It keeps the abstract noun sense.
items.exampleCN: 它保留抽象名词的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms similarly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 similarly。

items.example: The prefix dis- forms dissimilar.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 dis- 构成 dissimilar。

items.example: The prefix ad- forms assimilate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ad- 构成 assimilate。

definition_zh: 过于简化的；片面简单的；简单化的
definition_en: treating something more simply than it really is, so that important details or difficulties are lost
core_image: 一座删掉所有支撑的桥，只剩几条直棍撑着，一按就塌
scene: 一位新来的顾问在白板上画出五个箭头，说经济问题就靠这五步解决。The consultant offered a simplistic plan that ignored every local difficulty.
sceneCN: 这里 simplistic 是「过于简化的」（第 1 个义项：把复杂事情削得比它本身更简单）；句意：这位顾问提出了一份无视所有本地难处的过于简化的方案。

pos.zh: 形容词：过于简化的；片面简单的

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉批评性的形容词后缀 -istic 得到的基础形容词，义为「简单的；朴素的」，本身不带贬义
由 simple 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「简单；朴素」，是正面评价
由 simple 加动词后缀 -ify 构成，义为「简化」，本身中性，可好可坏
由 overly 的前缀 over- 加 simplify 构成，义为「过度简化」
由 simplify 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「简化；简化版」

senses.title: Too simple to be true
senses.definition: making a complicated matter seem simpler than it is, so that real details are ignored
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂的事情说得比实际简单，以致忽略了真实细节
senses.example: The article gives a simplistic picture of why the city floods every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章对该城每年春天为何内涝给出了一幅过于简化的图景。
senses.why: The suffix -istic marks a way of doing things, and here the simple way is pushed past the truth into a flaw.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -istic 标记一种做事方式，这里的「简单」被推过了真实的分寸，变成了缺陷。

senses.title: An oversimplified explanation
