senses.definition: explaining a cause or an event with one neat reason while leaving out other forces
senses.definitionCN: 用一条漂亮的原因解释事件，却漏掉其他起作用的力量
senses.example: Blaming the coach alone is a simplistic explanation for a poor season.
senses.exampleCN: 把糟糕的赛季只归因于教练，是一种过于简单的解释。
senses.why: A single cause is clean to say but leaves out everything else, and that gap is exactly what the word criticises.
senses.whyCN: 单一原因说起来干净利落，却漏掉了其余一切；这个词批评的正是这道缺口。

senses.title: An oversimplified solution
senses.definition: a plan or policy that promises a quick fix by looking only at a small part of the problem
senses.definitionCN: 只盯着问题的一小部分、却承诺快速见效的方案或政策
senses.example: Banning every car in the city centre is a simplistic solution to traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 禁止市中心所有汽车是对交通问题的简单化解决方案。
senses.why: From explanation the word moves to action: a plan built on a stripped-down model will fail where the model was wrong.
senses.whyCN: 从解释转向行动：建立在被削过的模型之上的方案，会在模型出错的地方失败。

senses.title: Dangerously simple thinking
senses.titleCN: 危险地过于简单的思维
senses.definition: a habit of thought that splits every question into two clean halves and admits no nuance
senses.definitionCN: 把每个问题都切成干净两半、不容任何细微差别的思维习惯
senses.example: Such simplistic thinking makes a real debate impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 这种过于简单的思维让真正的讨论无法进行。
senses.why: When the tendency to simplify lives in the mind rather than in one statement, the adjective shifts onto thinking itself.
senses.whyCN: 当简化的倾向住在头脑里而不是某句话里时，这个形容词就转移到思维本身之上。

senses.title: Simple and plain, without a sting
senses.titleCN: 朴素的；简单的（不带贬义）
senses.definition: in older and rarer use, plain or simple in a neutral or even positive way
senses.definitionCN: 在较早、较罕见的用法中，指朴素或简单，语气中性甚至正面
senses.example: Older books call a plainly built house simplistic, with no judgement implied.
senses.exampleCN: 旧书里会把一座盖得朴素的房子称作 simplistic，并不含贬意。
senses.why: Before the modern critical sense settled in, -istic simply meant in the manner of, so the word could praise plainness.
senses.whyCN: 在现代批评义稳固下来之前，-istic 只是「以……方式」的意思，所以这个词也可以赞美朴素。

senses.title: A deliberately compressed model
senses.definition: used in science or engineering for a model that is knowingly reduced to essentials for teaching or calculation
senses.definitionCN: 在科学或工程中，指为教学或计算而有意只保留要点的模型
senses.example: The diagram is simplistic on purpose, so that first-year students can follow it.
senses.exampleCN: 这张示意图是有意简化的，好让一年级学生看得懂。
senses.why: A simplification made with eyes open is a tool, not a failure, and the word can be used honestly in that frame.
senses.whyCN: 明知代价而做的简化是一种工具，而不是失败；在这一框架下这个词可用得不带讥讽。

intro.en: Simplistic is simpler plus the Latin-derived ending -istic, a combination that shifted from neutral plainness to the modern criticism of over-simplifying.
intro.cn: simplistic 是由 simpler 加上源自拉丁语的词尾 -istic 构成；这一组合从「朴素」的中性义转变成现代「过度简化」的批评义。

items.en: Simplex meant single, uncomplicated, one fold, and it described things that were not doubled or mixed. Its parts sim and plicare are generally accepted, though the exact early history of the word is not certain.
items.cn: simplex 意为「单一的、不复杂的一折」，用来描述不叠加、不混合的事物。一般认为它由 sim 与 plicare（折叠）两部分构成，但更早的确切历史并不确定。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, and it is behind a large Romanic family of like-sounding words with very different meanings. The link of simplex to plicare is an accepted but old and partly conjectural analysis.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」，是罗曼语族一大批音近而义远的词的来源。simplex 与 plicare 的联系一般认为成立，但这一分析古老且部分属推测。

items.en: Via French the word reached Middle English as simple, meaning plain, single, without ornament.
items.cn: 经由法语传入中古英语，成为 simple，义为「朴素的、单一的、无装饰的」。

items.en: Simpler was formed by adding the native comparative -er; the Greek-derived suffix -istic, present since the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, was then attached to make simplistic. The first printed dates are uncertain.
items.cn: simpler 由本族语的比较级词尾 -er 构成；十六、十七世纪起已有源自希腊语的后缀 -istic，再接到它上面就得到 simplistic。确切的最早印刷年代不确定。

items.en: In the twentieth century the negative sense of simplistic, too simple for the real difficulty, became the dominant one in debate and journalism.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，simplistic 的负面义「简单得配不上真实难度」在辩论与新闻中成为主流用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the simple, simplex root; the near-meaning group gathers words for plainness and shallow understanding, which differ in how much blame they carry.
note.cn: 形近组共享 simple、simplex 这一「一折、单一」词根；近义组收表示「朴素」与「浅薄理解」的一批词，它们的贬义轻重不同。

entries.definition: Easy to understand or do, or plain; the neutral base adjective, with no criticism built in.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「简单的、朴素的」，是中性的基础词，本身不带批评。

entries.definition: The quality of being simple, usually praised; having a lot of it is not the same as being simplistic.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「简单、朴素」，通常是褒义，与「简化过头」不同。

entries.definition: To make something easier to understand or do; neutral and often helpful.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「简化」，中性且往往有帮助。

entries.definition: Made too simple by leaving things out; close to simplistic but describes the result, not the habit.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被过度简化的」，与 simplistic 接近，但描述结果而非习惯。

entries.definition: Lacking experience or judgement; blames the person, while simplistic blames the idea.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「天真的、幼稚的」，批评的是人而不是观点。

entries.definition: Not going deep into a subject; broader and more blunt than simplistic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「浅薄的」，比 simplistic 更宽泛、更直白。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin base simplex, the suffix -istic, and the phrases the adjective actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词基 simplex、后缀 -istic，以及这个形容词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Add the critical ending -istic to simpler and you get the word that condemns a simplification.
normal.cn: 把带批评意味的词尾 -istic 加在 simpler 上，就得到指责「简化」的那个词。

normal.en: Simple is a compliment, but simplistic is an accusation, so do not use it when you mean easy.
normal.cn: simple 是称赞，simplistic 却是指控，想表达「容易」时千万别用后者。

normal.en: A simplistic view is a view that is not simple, it is too simple for the facts.
normal.cn: a simplistic view 并不是简单的看法，而是简单得配不上事实的看法。

normal.en: Simplify is neutral and helpful; the -istic ending adds the judgement that the simplification failed.
normal.cn: simplify 中性且有帮助；-istic 词尾则加上「这次简化失败了」的评判。

normal.en: Compare simplistic and simple: a simple plan can work, a simplistic plan has lost something it needed.
normal.cn: 对比 simplistic 与 simple：简单的计划可以奏效，过于简化的计划则丢掉了必需的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge drawn with only flat lines and no supports: it looks clean on paper and would fall at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座只画了平直线条、没有任何支撑的桥：纸上很好看，真造出来一按就塌。

abstract.en: Imagine a jigsaw with most of its pieces thrown away, then glued into a neat square anyway.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅拼图把大部分碎块都扔了，却照样粘成一个整齐的正方形。

abstract.en: Think of a cheap map that shows one straight road where the land is full of bends and rivers.
abstract.cn: 想象一张廉价地图，在满是弯道与河流的地方只画了一条直路。

examples.en: Critics say the film offers a simplistic view of rural life.
examples.cn: 评论家说这部电影呈现的乡村生活观过于简单。

examples.en: It would be simplistic to treat the disease as a matter of diet alone.
examples.cn: 把这种疾病只当作饮食问题来看会过于简单。

examples.en: The town rejected a simplistic plan to widen the only road through the centre.
examples.cn: 该镇否决了一项简单化的方案，即只拓宽穿过中心的唯一道路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「辛普利斯蒂克」——简单过头，简到丢东西：过于简化。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 simplex（单一的、不复杂的，字面「一折」）→ 经古法语 simple 进入中古英语 simple → 英语比较级 simpler → 加源自希腊语的后缀 -istic 得 simplistic。核心义「越过真相所需的简单，因而丢掉了必要细节」。simplex 与 plicare（折叠）的联系一般认为成立，但属于古老且部分推测的分析。

sensesIntro.en: Simplistic begins as criticism of a statement, then extends to explanations, solutions, a habit of mind, and finally to the rare neutral sense of plain, while a deliberately compressed model keeps the word blameless.
sensesIntro.cn: simplistic 从对一个说法的不满开始，延伸到解释、方案与思维习惯，最后还有一个罕见的「朴素」中性义；有意压缩的模型则让这个词免于指责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bridge drawn with straight lines but no supports, clean on paper and ready to collapse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座只由直线构成、没有任何支撑的桥，纸上干净利落，却随时会塌。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT: a description that strips away what made the matter hard in the first place.
branches.cn: 说法线：把原本让事情变难的要素都剥掉的描述。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: one neat reason takes the place of several interacting ones.
branches.cn: 原因线：一条漂亮的原因顶替了若干相互纠缠的原因。

branches.en: THE ACTION: a plan built on the stripped model, so it promises more than it can do.
branches.cn: 行动线：建立在被削过的模型之上的方案，承诺超出它的能力。

branches.en: THE MIND: the habit of splitting questions into halves without nuance.
branches.cn: 思维线：把问题一分为二、不容细微差别的习惯。

branches.en: THE EXEMPTIONS: the old neutral plainness, and the model reduced on purpose for teaching.
branches.cn: 豁免线：旧时中性的「朴素」义，以及为教学而有意压缩的模型。

intro.en: Simplistic is a family member built by suffixing: a Latin-fold base, an English comparison ending, and an ending that turns plain description into a judgement.
intro.cn: simplistic 是靠加词尾构成的家族成员：拉丁语「一折」词基、英语比较级词尾，再加上把朴素描述变成评判的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin simplex and plicare are recorded, but the analysis joining them is old and partly conjectural; -istic entered English from Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 simplex 与 plicare 均有文献记录，但把两者联系起来的分析古老且部分属推测；-istic 来自希腊语，经英语使用。

items.example: The Latin word means one fold.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词意为「一折」。

items.example: It appears in duplex and complex.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 duplex 与 complex 中。

items.example: French carried the adjective into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个形容词带进英语。

items.example: The comparison ending comes from native English.
items.exampleCN: 比较级词尾来自本族英语。

items.example: The suffix -istic forms simplistic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -istic 构成 simplistic。

items.example: The suffix -ify forms simplify.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ify 构成 simplify。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms simplicity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 simplicity。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms simplistically.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 simplistically。

items.example: The prefix over- forms oversimplify.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 over- 构成 oversimplify。

definition_zh: 肌腱；（复数）力量；元气；支柱；用肌腱加固
definition_en: a tendon that joins muscle to bone, or in the plural, strength, power, or the firm support of something
core_image: 小腿后侧一根绷紧的白亮筋束，把两端的骨头牢牢拉住
scene: 古代射手把弓拉到最大，小臂上的筋络一根根鼓起。The archer drew the bow until every sinew in his arm stood out.
sceneCN: 这里 sinew 是「肌腱」（第 1 个义项：把肌肉与骨头连起来、能绷紧发力的那根筋）；句意：射手把弓拉到极致，直到他手臂上的每根筋都凸了起来。

pos.zh: 名词：肌腱；筋；（复数）力量、元气、支柱
动词：用肌腱加固；使强健有力（多用过去分词）

collocations.zh: 一个国家的筋骨；国家的经济命脉
竭尽全力；拼命使出每一分力气
钢铁般的筋腱；极强健的体魄

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「多筋的；精瘦有力的；强健的」
由本词加后缀 -less 构成，义为「无筋的；无力的」，属罕见书面词
由本词加拉丁式后缀 -ous 构成，义为「多腱的；筋力强的」，属早期罕见形式

senses.title: A tendon joining muscle to bone
senses.definition: a tough cord or band of body tissue that attaches a muscle to a bone and carries its pull
senses.definitionCN: 连接肌肉与骨头、传递拉扯力的坚韧带状身体组织
senses.example: The surgeon repaired a torn sinew in the heel of the runner.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生修复了这名跑者脚跟上断裂的一根肌腱。
senses.why: Old English sinu already meant a tendon, and the word has kept that anatomical core for more than a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 sinu 本来就指肌腱，这个词一千多年来一直保留着这个解剖学核心义。

senses.title: Strength and physical power
senses.definition: the bodily vigour and power that such cords give, often spoken of in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 这些筋腱带来的身体元气与力量，常以复数形式出现
senses.example: The old athlete trained to keep the sinews of his legs working.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老运动员坚持训练，以保持双腿的筋力。
senses.why: The cord is the visible seat of pull, so the plural is used by extension for the power it produces.
senses.whyCN: 筋腱是拉扯力的可见所在，于是复数形式被用来转指它所发挥的力量。

senses.title: The means of power: the sinews of war
senses.titleCN: 力量的来源：战争的资源
senses.definition: in phrases such as the sinews of war, the money and supplies that keep an enterprise or army going
senses.definitionCN: 在「战争的资源」这类短语中，指维持一支军队或一项事业运转的金钱与物资
senses.example: In the seventeenth century money was called the sinews of war.
senses.exampleCN: 在十七世纪，金钱被称为战争的资源。
senses.why: A body needs tendons to move, and an army needs money to move, so the anatomical support became a metaphor for supply.
senses.whyCN: 身体要靠筋腱才能动，军队要靠钱才能动，于是生理上的支撑被比作补给。

senses.title: The strength that holds something together
senses.definition: the main source of vigour or cohesion in a group, economy, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 一个团体、经济或机构活力与凝聚力的主要来源
senses.example: Small firms are the sinews of the local economy.
senses.exampleCN: 小企业是当地经济的筋骨。
senses.why: Beyond war, the picture is reused wherever something needs a strong linkage to stay standing.
senses.whyCN: 除了战争，凡是需要强硬连接才能立住的事物，都会重新用上这幅图景。

senses.title: To strengthen and support
senses.definition: to brace or give strength and firm support to something, or to become sinewy
senses.definitionCN: 加固某物、给它力量与坚实支撑，或变得筋络强健
senses.example: The old planks were sinewed with new cords before the lifting.
senses.exampleCN: 这块旧木板在吊装之前用新绳子加固了。
senses.why: The rare verb turns the tendon into an action: put in the strength that makes a structure hold.
senses.whyCN: 这个罕见的动词把「筋腱」变成动作：把让结构立住的力量装进去。

intro.en: Sinew is one of the oldest English body words, recorded in Old English as sinu, and its journey is best followed through Germanic and Germanic-related forms.
intro.cn: sinew 是英语最古老的身体词之一，古英语写作 sinu；它的历史最好沿着日耳曼语族及相关形式来追。

items.en: A root generally reconstructed as *snēwō or *snewH-, meaning a tendon or cord, is widely cited, but the reconstruction and its exact shape are not settled.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个重构词根，写作 *snēwō 或 *snewH-，意为「肌腱、绳」。这一重构形式及其确切拼写并无定论。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed as *sinewō, meaning a tendon, from which the earliest English shape comes.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式重构为 *sinewō，意为「肌腱」，英语最早的形式由此而来。

items.en: Sinu is recorded in Old English meaning a tendon or band, and it also appears in compounds describing brawny strength.
items.cn: 古英语 sinu 有记录，意为「肌腱、筋带」，也见于描述强健筋力的复合词中。

items.en: The spelling settles as sineu and then sinew, and the plural begins to be used for strength and for the funds that keep power going.
items.cn: 拼写渐渐固定为 sineu、sinew，复数开始用于表示力量，以及维持权势所需的钱财。

items.en: Phrases such as the sinews of war become common in political prose; the exact first printed date is uncertain.
items.cn: the sinews of war 这类短语在政论文字中流行起来；确切的最早印刷年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English keeps the anatomy and the metaphor side by side, and adds an adjective, sinewy, that now describes lean physical strength.
items.cn: 现代英语让解剖义与比喻义并存，并加上形容词 sinewy，如今多形容精瘦有力的体态。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers tendon words; the near-meaning group gathers strength and support words whose pictures are different. Senile merely looks similar to sinew and comes from another root.
note.cn: 形近组收与「肌腱」同义或同族的词；近义组收表示力量与支撑的词，它们各自的画面并不相同。senile 与 sinew 只是拼写相近，词源不同，不计入本组。

entries.definition: The modern medical word for the same cord, drawn from Latin tendere, to stretch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肌腱」，是同一个部位在现代医学中的标准用词，源自拉丁语 tendere「伸展」。

entries.definition: Full of sinew or lean and wiry with strength, built directly from sinew with -y.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多筋的、精瘦有力的」，由本词直接加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: A similar body band, but one that links bone to bone rather than muscle to bone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「韧带」，是类似的带状组织，但连接的是骨头与骨头，而不是肌肉与骨头。

entries.definition: The general word for physical or other power; sinew is a narrower, fleshier picture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「力量」，是通用词；sinew 的画面更窄、更有肉身感。

entries.definition: Active, healthy energy, especially in body or in work; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「活力、精力」，指身体或工作中的充沛元气，语气正式。

entries.definition: The main support of a group or system, another body part turned into metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「骨干、支柱」，同样是把身体部位用作比喻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English shape sinu, the plural idiom, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语词形 sinu、复数习语，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Spell it out as sin plus ew and remember the Old English sinu, a body cord.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 sin 加 ew 来记，回想古英语 sinu 这个词，指的是一根身体里的筋。

normal.en: Strain every sinew is the idiom for trying as hard as the body allows.
normal.cn: strain every sinew 是「竭尽全力」的习语。

normal.en: The sinews of war has long been a phrase for money, because money moves armies as tendons move limbs.
normal.cn: the sinews of war 长久以来都是指钱的短语，因为钱带动军队，正如筋腱带动四肢。

normal.en: Add -y to get sinewy, the adjective for a lean, wiry body.
normal.cn: 加 -y 得到 sinewy，用来形容精瘦而有力的身体。

normal.en: Compare sinew with tendon: the two words name the same part, one from Old English, one from Latin.
normal.cn: 对比 sinew 与 tendon：两者指的是同一部位，一个来自古英语，一个来自拉丁语。

abstract.en: Picture a white cord pulled tight at the back of a calf, taking the weight of every step.
abstract.cn: 想象小腿后面一根被拉紧的白色筋束，承托着每一步的重量。

abstract.en: Imagine a map of a country drawn with thick lines where its roads, ports and factories are.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家的地图上，在道路、港口和工厂所在之处画着粗线。

abstract.en: Think of an army that cannot march without a cart of silver: the cart is what holds the body together.
abstract.cn: 想象一支没有一车银子就无法行军的军队：那车银子就是让身体立住的东西。

examples.en: The climber could feel the sinew in her shoulder tighten.
examples.cn: 攀岩者能感觉到肩膀里的筋绷紧了。

examples.en: He strained every sinew to finish the race after his fall.
examples.cn: 摔倒之后，他拼尽全力跑完了比赛。

examples.en: Historians describe taxation as the sinews of the early state.
examples.cn: 历史学家把征税称为早期国家的筋骨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「细纽」——手臂里那根又细又亮的纽绳，把骨头和肌肉扣在一起：筋腱。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 sinu（肌腱）→ 中古英语拼写渐定为 sinew；一般认为源自日耳曼语重构形式 *sinewō，更早可追溯到原始印欧语 *snēwō 或 *snewH-（肌腱、绳），但这一重构形式并无定论。核心义「把两端绷住的筋」。同族形容词 sinewy 表示「精瘦有力的」。

sensesIntro.en: Sinew runs from the anatomical cord to the strength it gives, then to the money that moves an army, the support that holds an economy up, and finally to a rare verb of bracing.
sensesIntro.cn: sinew 从解剖上的那根筋，到它带来的力量，再到推动军队的钱、撑起经济的支柱，最后是一个罕见的「加固」动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright white cord pulled tight behind the calf, holding bone and muscle together.
core.cn: 核心意象：小腿后侧一根绷紧的亮白筋束，把骨与肉牢牢连在一起。

branches.en: THE BODY: the physical cord itself, the sense the word has carried since Old English.
branches.cn: 身体线：那根实体筋腱，是这个词自古英语以来一直携带的义项。

branches.en: THE POWER: the pull of the cord becomes the vigour of the whole body, usually in the plural.
branches.cn: 力量线：筋腱的拉力变成整个身体的元气，通常用复数形式。

branches.en: THE WAR CHEST: what money does for an army is what tendons do for limbs.
branches.cn: 钱箱线：钱对军队的作用，正如筋腱对四肢的作用。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: any group or economy can be held together the same way.
branches.cn: 结构线：任何团体或经济都可以用同样的方式被撑住。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the rare verb puts the strength in, bracing what would otherwise give way.
branches.cn: 动作线：罕见的动词把力量装进去，加固本来会垮掉的东西。

intro.en: Sinew is a bare native root with almost no derivational machinery; the family is built only with common English endings.
intro.cn: sinew 是一个几乎没有构词附加成分的本族词根，这一词族只用常见的英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Sinew itself descends from Germanic forms rather than Latin, so no Latin ancestor is claimed; the Latin words shown here are related only by the later forms built on this word.
latinIntro.cn: sinew 本身来自日耳曼语形式而非拉丁语，因此不称它有拉丁语祖先；下面列出的是后来围绕这个词构成的词，并非其拉丁来源。

items.example: The Old English form is the earliest shape of the word.
items.exampleCN: 古英语形式是这个词最早的形态。

items.example: The noun keeps both the flesh and the force.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时保留了「筋」与「力」。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y forms sinewy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 sinewy。

items.example: Sinewy describes a wiry body.
items.exampleCN: sinewy 形容精瘦而有力的身体。

items.example: The suffix -less forms sinewless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 sinewless。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms sinewous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 sinewous。

items.meaning: strength, or the means of power
items.example: The plural carries the metaphor of strength.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式承载了「力量」的比喻义。

items.meaningCN: 以绳筋加固的；变强壮的
items.example: The participle is used as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词常被用作形容词。

latinEntries.meaning: a tendon, from tendere, to stretch
latinEntries.example: Tendo is a Latin synonym, not an ancestor of sinew.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tendo 是拉丁语同义词，并不是 sinew 的祖先。

definition_zh: 轻微燎焦；烧焦（毛发、衣物或食物边缘）；被燎焦
definition_en: to burn the surface or the edges of something lightly, slightly, or unevenly
core_image: 火苗一舔，布角或头发边缘焦卷发黄，却没有真正烧穿
scene: 餐馆后厨，厨师探身去够高处的香料罐，围裙下摆扫过灶台的蓝色火苗。The flame singed the edge of her apron before she pulled it away.
sceneCN: 这里 singe 是「燎焦边缘」（第 1 个义项：只把表面或边缘烧焦）；句意：她还没把围裙拉开，火苗已经把围裙边燎焦了。

pos.zh: 轻微烧焦；燎焦（毛发、衣物、食物边缘）

derivatives.zh: 在 singe 后加名词后缀 -ing，指「燎焦、烧毛」这一过程
过去分词转形容词，指「被燎焦的」，如燎焦的眉毛

senses.title: To burn the surface lightly
senses.definition: to burn the surface or the edges of something slightly, so that it is scorched but not seriously damaged
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的表面或边缘轻轻烧焦，形成焦痕但不造成严重损坏
senses.example: The hot pan singed the cloth on the edge of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 滚烫的锅把桌边那块布燎焦了。
senses.why: The core image is a flame that only licks the surface, so the basic sense keeps the idea of a light, partial burn.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是火苗只舔到表面，因此基本义保留「轻、局部地烧到」的意思，而不指烧穿或烧毁。

senses.title: To scorch hair or fur
senses.definition: to burn the ends of hair, fur, or feathers and make them curl or smell scorched
senses.definitionCN: 把头发、兽毛或羽毛的末端烧到卷曲、发黄或带焦味
senses.example: She leaned too close to the candle and singed her hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她凑蜡烛太近，把头发燎到了。
senses.why: Hair and fur are the thinnest, most exposed edge anyone has, so the surface-burning image attaches to them first and most vividly.
senses.whyCN: 头发和兽毛是最薄、最暴露的「边缘」，所以燎表面这个意象最先也最生动地落到毛发上。

senses.title: To burn something off the skin
senses.definition: to remove hair or bristles by passing a flame quickly over the skin
senses.definitionCN: 用火焰快速扫过皮肤或皮面，把上面的毛或鬃烧掉
senses.example: In old kitchens, the cook would singe a chicken to remove the small feathers.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的厨房里，厨师会燎一下鸡，去掉细毛。
senses.why: If the flame only touches the surface, the surface layer can be removed while the flesh beneath stays intact, which turns the burn into a cleaning action.
senses.whyCN: 既然火只碰到表面，那么表层被烧掉而下面的肉完好，这一「烧表面」就转化成了清洁去毛的动作。

senses.title: To scorch food slightly
senses.definition: to give food a light, browned scorch, usually on purpose, before it is cooked further
senses.definitionCN: 把食物表面烤出浅浅的焦痕，通常是有意为之，以便继续烹调
senses.example: Chefs singe peppers over a gas burner before chopping them.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师会先把甜椒在燃气灶上燎焦，再切碎。
senses.why: Deliberate light burning adds the smoky, charred flavour, so the same surface scorch becomes a cooking technique rather than damage.
senses.whyCN: 故意轻微地烧焦能带来烟熏焦香，于是同样的「燎表面」从损坏变成了烹饪手法。

senses.title: To affect something slightly and badly
senses.titleCN: 轻微地损害；留下小小的焦痕
senses.definition: to damage something small in a limited way, often so that the mark is all that remains
senses.definitionCN: 小范围地损害某物，通常只留下一点痕迹
senses.example: The explosion singed the edges of the documents but left the text readable.
senses.exampleCN: 爆炸燎焦了文件边缘，但文字仍可辨认。
senses.why: Because the burn is only on the surface, the figurative step is small: a slight, visible harm that stops short of destroying what it touches.
senses.whyCN: 因为烧的只是表面，比喻义的跨度也很小：一种轻微、看得见的伤害，恰恰止步于毁坏之前。

senses.title: To be scorched
senses.definition: of hair, cloth, or food, to become slightly burnt
senses.definitionCN: 头发、布料或食物被轻轻烧到
senses.example: The scarf singed as it brushed the edge of the campfire.
senses.exampleCN: 围巾擦过篝火边缘时被燎焦了。
senses.why: The intransitive form simply drops the person doing the burning and lets the surface, not the flame, be the subject.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法只是去掉了「谁在烧」这个施动者，让承受者（表面）而不是火焰成为句子的主语。

senses.title: A scorch mark
senses.definition: a slight burn mark left on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 留在表面上的一处轻微烧焦痕迹
senses.example: There is a small singe on the table near the candle.
senses.exampleCN: 蜡烛旁的桌面上有一处小小的燎痕。
senses.why: Once an action leaves a visible mark, the word can name the mark itself, which is the usual path from verb to noun.
senses.whyCN: 动作一旦留下可见痕迹，这个词就可以直接指那道痕迹，这是动词转名词最常见的路径。

senses.title: A slight effect or a narrow escape
senses.definition: a small, limited impact on someone or something, especially one that just misses being serious
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物造成的轻微、有限的波及，尤其是险些严重却只是擦过的情形
senses.example: The company was only singed by the scandal, not ruined by it.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司只是被丑闻轻微波及，并未因此垮掉。
senses.why: The idea of a burn that lands on the edge and stops there makes a natural metaphor for damage that brushes a person or firm and then withdraws.
senses.whyCN: 「烧到边缘就停」的画面，天然可以比喻伤害只是擦过某人或某家机构，随即退去。

intro.en: Singe comes from Old English sengan, to scorch or burn lightly, and is not related to the word sing.
intro.cn: singe 来自古英语 sengan，意为轻微烧灼，与单词 sing 没有词源关系。

items.en: Sengan means to scorch or burn the surface of something.
items.cn: sengan 意为燎焦某物的表面。

items.en: The verb appears in the Middle English form sengen, still with the sense of burning lightly.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语中写作 sengen，仍保留轻微烧灼之义。

items.en: The modern spelling singe settles, and the word is used for burning hair and feathers.
items.cn: 现代拼写 singe 固定下来，并被用来指燎毛发、去禽毛。

items.en: The noun singe appears for a scorch mark, and kitchen use of singeing chicken or game spreads.
items.cn: 表示焦痕的名词 singe 出现，厨房里燎鸡、燎野味的用法也逐渐普及。

items.en: Modern English keeps singe for light, surface burns and extends it to figurative small damage.
items.cn: 现代英语继续用 singe 表示表面的轻烧，并把它扩展到比喻义上的轻微损害。

note.en: Singe sits beside words for burning, with burn and scorch as the nearest meaning, and sing, fringed, and sting as look-alikes.
note.cn: singe 处在「燃烧」词群里，近义是 burn 与 scorch，形近的是 sing、fringed 与 sting。

entries.definition: to make musical sounds with the voice
entries.definitionCN: 唱歌；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to hurt someone with a sharp point or poisoned part
entries.definitionCN: 刺；蜇；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a tall grass-like plant that grows in wet ground
entries.definitionCN: 莎草；只是拼写相近、发音相同，词源不同

entries.definition: to be damaged or destroyed by fire or heat
entries.definitionCN: 烧；烧毁（范围最大，可严重可轻微）

entries.definition: to burn the surface and change its colour, without catching fire
entries.definitionCN: 烤焦；烫焦（程度比 singe 重，颜色变化明显）

entries.definition: to blacken something by burning it partly
entries.definitionCN: 烧黑；炭化（表面变黑且更彻底）

normalIntro.en: Singe is about the flame that only grazes the surface: the edge of cloth, hair, or food goes brown and curls but does not burn through.
normalIntro.cn: singe 说的是只擦过表面的火：布边、头发或食物的边被燎黄、卷起，但并没有烧穿。

normal.en: Keep singe and sing apart: singe has an e at the end, and it has nothing to do with music.
normal.cn: 把 singe 和 sing 分开：singe 词尾多一个 e，它与唱歌毫无关系。

normal.en: The past tense is singed, and the e is kept because of the soft g sound.
normal.cn: 过去式是 singed，保留字母 e 是为了让 g 仍读软音。

normal.en: Singeing keeps the e before the -ing ending, so the g stays soft.
normal.cn: 加 -ing 时 singeing 仍保留 e，g 才能维持软音。

normal.en: The verb usually takes a part: singe your hair, singe the edges, singe the fabric.
normal.cn: 这个动词常接某个部位：燎到头发、燎焦边缘、燎焦布料。

normal.en: Compare scorch and char: singe is the lightest of the three, scorch darkens the surface, and char blackens and hardens it.
normal.cn: 对比 scorch 与 char：singe 最轻，scorch 使表面变色，char 则烧黑发硬。

abstract.en: Picture the darkest corner on the left-hand side, where sinister keeps its origin.
abstract.cn: 想象烛火轻轻擦过一个信封的角。

abstract.en: Imagine the blue flame of a stove sweeping the short hairs on your forearm.
abstract.cn: 想象灶台的蓝色火苗扫过小臂上的汗毛。

abstract.en: Think of a cook turning a plucked chicken over a burner so the fine feathers curl away.
abstract.cn: 想象厨师在灶火上翻转一只拔过毛的鸡，让细毛卷掉。

examples.en: The iron was too hot and singed the collar of the shirt.
examples.cn: 熨斗太烫，把衬衫领子燎焦了。

examples.en: He singed his eyebrows when the match flared up.
examples.cn: 火柴突然窜起火焰，燎到了他的眉毛。

examples.en: Keep the paper away from the flame or the edges will singe.
examples.cn: 把纸远离火焰，否则边缘会被燎焦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森急」——深夜做饭火太大，一「急」就把菜边「燎」焦了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 sengan（轻微烧灼）→ 中古英语 sengen → 现代拼写 singe；没有可靠的拉丁语来源，核心义为「火只舔到表面」。

sensesIntro.en: Singe moves from a light surface burn to hair and feathers, to burning hair off, to deliberate cooking scorch, and finally to small damage and a visible scorch mark.
sensesIntro.cn: singe 从表面的轻烧出发，过渡到毛发与羽毛，再到燎掉表面毛发，继而成为烹饪中的故意燎焦，最后引申为轻微损害和留下的焦痕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flame that only grazes the surface of cloth, hair, or skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：火苗只擦过布、头发或皮肤的极薄表面。

branches.en: The light surface burn is the direct and central sense.
branches.cn: 表面的轻烧是直接而核心的义项。

branches.en: Hair and fur catch the flame first because they are the thinnest exposed surfaces.
branches.cn: 毛发最先被火烧到，因为它们是最薄、最暴露的表面。

branches.en: Burning a surface can be a cleaning step or a cooking technique.
branches.cn: 燎烧表面既可以是清洁步骤，也可以是烹饪手法。

branches.en: A burn that stays on the surface becomes a metaphor for limited harm.
branches.cn: 止于表面的灼烧，被用作有限损害的比喻。

branches.en: The state, the mark, and the figurative trace all grow from the same visible scorch.
branches.cn: 被烧的状态、留下的痕迹以及比喻义的余痕，都出自同一道可见的焦痕。

intro.en: Singe is a native English verb with little affixation: the family is built with -ed, -ing, and a few compounds such as hair-singeing.
intro.cn: singe 是本土英语动词，构词很少：词族靠 -ed、-ing 以及 hair-singeing 这类复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Singe is not Latin in origin; its Old English source is usually linked to a Germanic base meaning to burn or cauterise, recorded as a reconstructed form.
latinIntro.cn: singe 并非来自拉丁语；其古英语源头一般认为与「烧、烙」的日耳曼语词干有关，以重构形式记录，拉丁语中并无对应词族。

items.example: Sengan is the recorded Old English ancestor of singe.
items.exampleCN: sengan 是 singe 有文献记载的古英语前身。

items.example: Singe keeps the light-burn sense today.
items.exampleCN: singe 至今保留轻烧的意思。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms the past tense singed.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成过去式 singed。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms the process noun singeing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成过程名词 singeing。

items.meaning: a person or device that does it
items.example: The suffix -er would give a rare agent noun, not common in this family.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 虽可构成施事名词，但在这个词族里并不常用。

items.example: The compound hair-singeing appears in salons and barbershops.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 hair-singeing 见于美发与理发场合。

items.example: The adjective singed describes a smell or an edge.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 singed 用来形容气味或边缘。

items.example: The noun singe names the mark left behind.
items.exampleCN: 名词 singe 指留下的焦痕。

items.meaning: the act of burning the surface
items.example: Keep the e in singeing so the g stays soft.
items.exampleCN: singeing 保留 e，让 g 保持软音。

definition_zh: 邪恶的；不吉利的；阴险的；（纹章学）左侧的
definition_en: seeming evil or threatening, especially in a way that suggests harm or bad luck is coming
core_image: 昏暗中从左侧慢慢伸过来的一只手，掌心向上，让人本能地往后一缩
scene: 雨夜的老楼走廊尽头没有开灯，一个陌生人一动不动地站在阴影里，只露出一侧肩膀的轮廓。A sinister figure waited in the unlit corridor until the door closed behind her.
sceneCN: 这里 sinister 是「邪恶而不祥的」（第 2 个义项：令人感到威胁、邪恶的）；句意：她身后的门一关上，一个阴森可怕的身影就等在没开灯的走廊里。

derivatives.zh: 在 sinister 后加 -al，指「左侧的；惯用左手的」，保留原义的方位色彩
由拉丁语词根加 -ose 构成，指（植物）向左旋的
由 sinistral 加 -ity 构成，指「惯用左手；左利手」

senses.title: On the left side
senses.definition: of, on, or belonging to the left side, used chiefly in heraldry and old technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 位于左侧、属于左边的，主要用于纹章学和早期学术写作
senses.example: In heraldry, the sinister side of a shield is the bearer left.
senses.exampleCN: 在纹章学中，盾牌的左侧指的是持盾者的左方。
senses.why: The Latin word means left, so the oldest sense is purely positional, and the dark meanings came later.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在拉丁语里本就意为「左」，所以最早的义项纯粹是方位性的，阴暗的含义是后来才叠加的。

senses.title: Evil or threatening
senses.titleCN: 邪恶的；令人感到威胁的
senses.definition: seeming evil, harmful, or menacing, often without saying so openly
senses.definitionCN: 显得邪恶、有害或咄咄逼人，往往并不明说
senses.example: A sinister figure stood at the end of the dark corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊尽头的黑暗处站着一个阴森可怕的身影。
senses.why: Because the left hand was long thought unlucky or untrustworthy, anything placed on the left side came to feel menacing.
senses.whyCN: 因为左手长期被认为不吉利、不可信，凡被放到「左侧」的事物也就渐渐显得有威胁。

senses.title: Giving a warning of bad luck
senses.definition: suggesting that something bad is about to happen, often through an omen or a hidden detail
senses.definitionCN: 暗示即将发生坏事，常通过征兆或隐藏的细节来传达
senses.example: The dark clouds on the horizon were a sinister warning of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 天边的乌云是暴风雨将至的不祥征兆。
senses.why: The same left-side omen idea becomes a general signal of coming harm, attached to weather, signs, and events.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「左边为凶」的预兆观念，泛化为对即将到来的伤害的预示，可用在天气、征兆与事件上。

senses.title: Cunning and deceptive
senses.definition: acting in a secretive, indirect way in order to do harm
senses.definitionCN: 以隐秘、间接的方式行事以便加害他人
senses.example: There was something sinister in the way he kept changing the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他不断转移话题的样子透着一种阴险。
senses.why: The link between the left and the crooked is old, so a hidden, sideways move of the mind picks up the same word.
senses.whyCN: 「左」与「歪斜不正」的关联由来已久，因此思想上的隐秘、绕弯动作也沿用了同一个词。

senses.title: Baleful magic or sorcery
senses.titleCN: 带有邪恶魔法的；妖异的
senses.definition: belonging to magic, spells, or powers that are meant to harm
senses.definitionCN: 属于旨在害人的法术、咒语或力量
senses.example: The old book was full of sinister spells and drawings of horns.
senses.exampleCN: 那本古书里满是妖异的咒语和画着犄角的图案。
senses.why: The left hand has been linked to witches and ill omens for centuries, so occult harm settles naturally on this word.
senses.whyCN: 几个世纪以来左手一直被与女巫和凶兆联系在一起，因此隐秘的害人之力自然落在这个词上。

senses.title: Inauspicious or unlucky
senses.definition: bringing or announcing bad fortune, often as a formal omen
senses.definitionCN: 带来或宣告厄运，常指正式的凶兆
senses.example: The birds flying to the left were seen as a sinister sign.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟儿向左飞被看作凶兆。
senses.why: Roman augurs read birds on the left as unfavourable, and that omen sense survives in the word today.
senses.whyCN: 罗马占卜师把左方出现的飞鸟视为不吉，这一预兆义至今仍留在词里。

senses.title: Deliberately left-handed or bent
senses.definition: bent or turning toward the left, as in some plants and heraldic bands
senses.definitionCN: 向左弯曲或向左旋的，如某些植物和纹章中的斜带
senses.example: A sinister bend runs from the top of the shield to the lower left corner.
senses.exampleCN: 一道左斜带从盾牌顶端延伸向左下角。
senses.why: The strict positional left sense survives in technical naming, where the shield or the plant is described exactly.
senses.whyCN: 严格的方位义在专业命名中保留了下来，用于精确描述盾面或植物的走向。

senses.title: A feeling that something is wrong
senses.definition: describing an atmosphere or detail that makes people uneasy without any open cause
senses.definitionCN: 形容某种气氛或细节，没有明显理由就让人不安
senses.example: There was a sinister quiet in the office after the staff left.
senses.exampleCN: 员工离开后，办公室里弥漫着令人不安的寂静。
senses.why: Threat does not need an agent: a hint of the left, the hidden, and the coming harm is enough to unsettle a whole room.
senses.whyCN: 威胁不一定需要一个主体：只要有一丝「偏向、藏匿、将至」的暗示，就足以让整间屋子不安。

intro.en: Sinister is Latin for left, and its change from left to evil reflects the old European habit of treating the left side as unlucky.
intro.cn: sinister 在拉丁语中意为「左」，它从「左」变成「邪恶」，反映了欧洲旧时把左侧视为不吉的习惯。

items.en: Sinister is the ordinary Latin adjective for left, and it is also used for auspices considered unfavourable.
items.cn: sinister 是拉丁语中常用的「左手边」，也用于指被视为不利的预兆。

items.en: Roman augurs watched birds on the left and read them as sign of ill fortune, which strengthens the bad omen sense.
items.cn: 罗马占卜师观察从左侧飞来的鸟，并把它读作凶兆，这加深了「不祥」的意思。

items.en: The word enters English through Old French with the sense of left side, especially in heraldry.
items.cn: 这个词经由古法语进入英语，先指「左侧」，多用于纹章学。

items.en: By the early modern period it commonly means evil, unlucky, and dishonest.
items.cn: 到了近代早期，它已普遍表示邪恶、不吉利和不正当。

items.en: Modern English keeps the threat sense as the dominant one and reserves the literal left sense for heraldry and biology.
items.cn: 现代英语以「威胁、邪恶」为主要义项，字面的「左」只保留在纹章学与生物学中。

note.en: Sinister looks like the left-hand words sinistral and sinistrality, and its meaning neighbours are evil, ominous, and malevolent.
note.cn: sinister 形近于表示「左侧」的 sinistral 与 sinistrality，意义上则与 evil、ominous 和 malevolent 相邻。

entries.definition: of or on the left side, or left-handed
entries.definitionCN: 左侧的；惯用左手的（保留拉丁语「左」的本义）

entries.definition: the state of being left-handed
entries.definitionCN: 左利手；惯用左手

entries.definition: genuine and free from pretence
entries.definitionCN: 真诚的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: morally very bad
entries.definitionCN: 邪恶的（更直接、更强烈）

entries.definition: suggesting that something bad will happen
entries.definitionCN: 不祥的；预兆不吉的

entries.definition: wanting to cause harm to others
entries.definitionCN: 恶意的；心怀恶念的

normalIntro.en: Sinister once simply meant left, and because the left side was thought unlucky, the word turned into a sign of threat.
normalIntro.cn: sinister 原本只表示「左」，因为左侧被认为不吉利，这个词后来才变成威胁的标记。

normal.en: The Latin source is sinister, left, and the same root gives sinistral, on the left.
normal.cn: 拉丁语原词是 sinister，意为「左」，同一词根还构成表示「左侧」的 sinistral。

normal.en: Remember the pattern with dexter, right: dexterous describes skill, while sinister describes doom.
normal.cn: 记住与 dexter（右）的对照：dexterous 形容灵巧，sinister 则形容凶险。

normal.en: In heraldry, sinister still means left, so a sinister bend goes toward the lower left.
normal.cn: 在纹章学中，sinister 仍指左侧，所以左斜带是朝左下延伸的。

normal.en: Combine the word with nouns of motive and mood: sinister motive, sinister smile, sinister silence.
normal.cn: 把它与表示动机和气氛的名词搭配：险恶动机、阴险的笑、令人不安的寂静。

normal.en: Distinguish ominous: ominous warns that something bad will come, while sinister says that it already looks evil.
normal.cn: 与 ominous 区分：ominous 警告坏事将至，sinister 则说某物本身就显出邪恶。

abstract.en: Picture the dark left-hand corner of a bad to echo the Latin sense of left.
abstract.cn: 对比拉丁语「左」，想象阴影最深的左角。

abstract.en: Imagine a hooded shape at the end of a hallway, standing just out of the light.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊尽头一个戴兜帽的身影，恰恰站在灯光之外。

abstract.en: Think of an old weather sign on a stormy morning and remember that omens also came from the left.
abstract.cn: 想象暴风雨早晨的旧时天气征兆，并记住凶兆也来自左侧。

examples.en: There was a sinister silence in the house after the lights went out.
examples.cn: 灯灭之后，屋子里出现一种令人不安的寂静。

examples.en: The film gives the story a sinister twist in its final scene.
examples.cn: 影片在最后一场戏里给故事添上了一层邪恶的转折。

examples.en: Scholars still argue whether the old omen was read as sinister or favourable.
examples.cn: 学者们至今仍有争议：那个古老的预兆究竟被视为凶兆还是吉兆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死你死的」——听着就透着邪恶与不祥，好事的词不会这样发音；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sinister（左；不利的预兆）→ 古法语 sinistre → 英语 sinister；同源的 sinistral 仍保留「左」的本义，核心义由「左」转向「阴暗、不祥」。

sensesIntro.en: Sinister starts as a strict left-side word, then gathers senses of threat, ill omen, cunning, sorcery, bad luck, technical leftward bending, and a general sense of unease.
sensesIntro.cn: sinister 先是严格的方位词「左」，随后发展出威胁、凶兆、阴险、邪术、不吉、技术性的向左弯曲，以及泛指的令人不安等义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that comes in from the left, low and slow, just out of sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只从左侧探过来、又低又慢的手，仿佛就在视线之外。

branches.en: The literal left sense survives in heraldry and technical use.
branches.cn: 字面的「左」义保留在纹章学与技术性用法中。

branches.en: Evil and cunning are the everyday moral senses.
branches.cn: 邪恶与阴险是日常最常用的道德义项。

branches.en: The omen and unlucky senses came straight from Roman augury.
branches.cn: 预兆与不吉的义项直接来自罗马占卜。

branches.en: Sorcery extends the omen into harmful magic.
branches.cn: 邪术义把凶兆扩展到害人的法力。

branches.en: Technical leftward bending and unsettled atmosphere are two late offshoots.
branches.cn: 技术性的向左弯曲与令人不安的气氛是两个较晚的旁支。

intro.en: Sinister carries a Latin root and now builds mainly technical words such as sinistral and sinistrorse.
intro.cn: sinister 带有拉丁语词根，如今主要构成 sinistral、sinistrorse 这类技术词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sinister means left, and its pair dexter means right; the left word took on the bad meanings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sinister 意为「左」，与之相对的 dexter 意为「右」；是「左」这个词承担了负面含义。

items.example: In Latin, sinister is simply the left hand side.
items.exampleCN: 在拉丁语里，sinister 就是左手边。

items.example: Dexter is the right-hand counterpart of sinister.
items.exampleCN: dexter 是 sinister 相对的「右」。

items.example: Sinistral keeps the literal left sense alive.
items.exampleCN: sinistral 让字面的「左」义延续下来。

items.example: Sinistrality is studied in neurology.
items.exampleCN: sinistrality 是神经学的研究对象。

items.example: Sinistrorse describes a climbing plant that winds anticlockwise.
items.exampleCN: sinistrorse 形容逆时针盘绕的攀援植物。

items.example: Dexterous comes from dexter, the right hand.
items.exampleCN: dexterous 来自表示右手的 dexter。

items.example: The suffix -al forms sinistral from this root.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 由该词根构成 sinistral。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms sinistrality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 sinistrality。

items.example: The suffix -ose forms sinistrorse.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ose 构成 sinistrorse。

definition_zh: 小口喝；抿；一小口的量
definition_en: to drink something slowly in small amounts, taking a little at a time
core_image: 嘴唇贴着杯沿，只让一小口热茶流进来，然后停住等它变凉
scene: 宴会刚开始，主人举着杯子礼貌地示意，却并不急着喝，只是让杯沿贴住下唇停了一下。She sipped her coffee slowly while the guests talked.
sceneCN: 这里 sip 是「小口喝、抿」（第 1 个义项：小口慢慢地喝）；句意：客人们聊天时，她的咖啡只是一小口一小口地抿着。

derivatives.zh: 在 sip 后加 -er，指「小口喝的人」或带吸管的杯子
由 sip 加 -y 构成，用于 sippy cup，指幼儿用的防漏学饮杯
在 sip 后加 -ing，指「一小口一小口地喝」的动作或过程

senses.title: To drink in small amounts
senses.definition: to drink something a little at a time, taking small amounts slowly
senses.definitionCN: 一点一点地喝，慢慢地把少量液体送入口中
senses.example: She sipped the hot soup until it cooled down.
senses.exampleCN: 她一小口一小口地喝热汤，直到汤凉下来。
senses.why: The word imitates the small, sharp movement of lips drawing a little liquid, so the basic sense is drinking in tiny amounts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿嘴唇吸进一点点液体时那种小而短促的动作，所以基本义就是「一点点地喝」。

senses.title: To take a little at a time from a drink
senses.definition: to drink from a cup or glass gradually, often without finishing it
senses.definitionCN: 从杯子或玻璃杯里渐渐喝，往往并不喝完
senses.example: He only held the glass all evening and never took a single sip.
senses.exampleCN: 整晚他一口都没喝，只是握着杯子。
senses.why: Because each motion is short and repeated, the action easily stretches over a long time, producing the sense of slowly working through a drink.
senses.whyCN: 因为每次动作都短促而重复，这个动作很容易延续很长时间，于是产生「慢慢喝完一杯」的意思。

senses.title: To taste with care
senses.definition: to drink slowly so as to taste or judge a drink, especially wine or tea
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢喝以便品味或判断饮品，尤指酒或茶
senses.example: The judge sipped the wine and wrote down her comments.
senses.exampleCN: 评审抿了一口葡萄酒，写下了她的评语。
senses.why: Sipping keeps a drink in the mouth long enough to feel it, so the small-motion drink becomes an act of tasting and judging.
senses.whyCN: 小口抿能让饮品在口中停留足够久以感受风味，这种小动作的喝法于是变成了品味与评断。

senses.title: To take a small, slow action
senses.definition: to do or use something in small doses, especially as a way of making it last
senses.definitionCN: 以少量、多次的方式做某事或使用某物，尤为了让它持续更久
senses.example: She sipped her savings through the long winter.
senses.exampleCN: 整个漫长的冬天，她一点一点地用着存款。
senses.why: The image of tiny repeated amounts transfers to anything that is taken slowly, from money to attention.
senses.whyCN: 少量而重复的画面可以迁移到任何「慢慢地消耗」的事物上，从钱到注意力都可以。

senses.title: A small amount of drink
senses.definition: a very small quantity of liquid taken into the mouth at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次入口的极少量液体
senses.example: He took a sip from her glass and set it down.
senses.exampleCN: 他从她的杯子里抿了一口，然后放下。
senses.why: One short draw of the lips is a countable event, so the action becomes the measured unit of the drink itself.
senses.whyCN: 一次短促的吸抿是可数的一次事件，于是动作本身就成了计量饮品的最小单位。

senses.title: A weak or unimportant thing
senses.titleCN: 微不足道的一句话或一点
senses.definition: something small, weak, or barely noticeable, often used with a negative to mean none at all
senses.definitionCN: 某种很小、很弱或几乎察觉不到的事物，常与否定词连用表示「一点也没有」
senses.example: There was not a sip of truth in the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一点工作上的贡献都没有给他。
senses.why: Because a sip is the smallest possible unit of a drink, the phrase can mean the least amount of anything at all.
senses.whyCN: 因为抿一口是饮品的最小单位，这个说法就可以用来指任何事物中最少的一点。

intro.en: Sip is an imitative English verb, first recorded in the Middle English period, and it may be linked to the small sucking movement.
intro.cn: sip 是英语中的拟声动词，最早见于中古英语时期，一般认为与嘴唇小口吸的动作有关。

items.en: The verb sip is first recorded, meaning to drink a little at a time.
items.cn: 动词 sip 最早被记录，意为一点一点地喝。

items.en: The noun sip appears for a small amount of drink.
items.cn: 表示「一小口的量」的名词 sip 出现。

items.en: Sip is used for a slow, unhurried way of drinking, and phrases such as sipping wine spread.
items.cn: sip 被用来表示缓慢从容的喝法，讲究「慢抿」的饮酒说法流行开来。

items.en: Sipping tools and sipping cups appear, and the word takes on the idea of a measured dose.
items.cn: 讲究小口喝的杯具出现，这个词也带上了「量小而克制」的意味。

items.en: Modern English uses sip for drinks, for tasting, and figuratively for anything taken slowly.
items.cn: 现代英语用 sip 指饮料、品鉴，也比喻任何慢慢「一点一点」的消耗。

note.en: Sip looks like the short words sip, pie, and siphon, and it sits next to drink, gulp, and quaff on the scale of how fast you drink.
note.cn: sip 形近于 pie 与 siphon，意义上处在表示喝速的 drink、gulp 与 quaff 这一序列中。

entries.definition: the side of the body below the waist
entries.definitionCN: 髋部；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the pointed end of something, or extra money for service
entries.definitionCN: 尖端；小费；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a tube used to draw liquid from one container to another
entries.definitionCN: 虹吸管；与 sip 共享「小口吸」的拟声联想，但词源关系存疑

entries.definition: to take liquid into the body
entries.definitionCN: 喝（最中性、范围最广）

entries.definition: to swallow a large amount quickly
entries.definitionCN: 大口咽下；猛喝（与 sip 相反的动作）

entries.definition: to drink a large amount in long swallows
entries.definitionCN: 畅饮；豪饮（文学性较强）

normalIntro.en: Sip is a tiny drink: the lips take only a little, the cup stays in the hand, and the motion is repeated slowly.
normalIntro.cn: sip 是极小的喝：嘴唇只吸取一点点，杯子一直握在手里，动作被缓慢地重复。

normal.en: Remember the double consonant: sipped and sipping double the p, and sips does not.
normal.cn: 注意双写辅音：过去式 sipped 与现在分词 sipping 双写 p，三单 sips 则不双写。

normal.en: The usual structure is sip at something, taking small amounts rather than a full mouthful.
normal.cn: 常见结构是 sip at something，表示一小口一小口地取，而不是满满一口。

normal.en: Take a sip is the standard noun phrase; it means one small mouthful.
normal.cn: take a sip 是标准的名词搭配，表示抿一口、喝一小口。

normal.en: Compare the pair: sip for the smallest amount, drink for the ordinary act, gulp for the largest.
normal.cn: 对比这三个词：sip 量最小，drink 是中性的常规动作，gulp 量最大。

normal.en: Sipping wine and sipping tea are the classic collocations, both suggesting slow and careful tasting.
normal.cn: sipping wine 与 sipping tea 是经典搭配，都暗示缓慢而仔细的品味。

abstract.en: Picture a straw in a cold drink, drawing up just a little liquid.
abstract.cn: 想象一根吸管伸进冰饮，只抽上一点点液体。

abstract.en: Imagine a cup lifted but not tilted, the surface of the tea barely moving.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子被举起却几乎没有倾斜，茶面几乎不动。

abstract.en: Think of a tasting glass passed around a table, each person only wetting their lips.
abstract.cn: 想象一只品酒杯在桌边传过，每个人只是润一下嘴唇。

examples.en: She sipped her tea while reading the morning paper.
examples.cn: 她一边看晨报，一边小口喝茶。

examples.en: Take a sip of water before you speak.
examples.cn: 开口之前先喝一小口水。

examples.en: The children were told not to gulp their juice but to sip it slowly.
examples.cn: 孩子们被告知别猛灌果汁，要慢慢地小口喝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吸噗」——嘴唇轻轻一「吸」，发一声「噗」，就是抿一口；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 sip（拟声词，源于小口吸啜的动作）→ 现代英语 sip；一般认为模仿嘴唇吸取液体的短促声响，没有可靠的拉丁语词根。

sensesIntro.en: Sip begins with the physical act of taking a little liquid, grows into slow drinking and careful tasting, then moves to slow small consumption in general and finally to the countable sip and the smallest possible amount.
sensesIntro.cn: sip 从「咽下一小口液体」的生理动作出发，扩展为慢喝与细品，再到泛指缓慢少量的消耗，最后成为可数名词「一小口」以及「最少的一点」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lips taking a few drops of liquid and pausing before the next drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：嘴唇先吸进几滴液体，停一下，再吸下一小口。

branches.en: The basic physical act is drinking in small amounts.
branches.cn: 最基本的生理动作就是小口地喝。

branches.en: Slow drinking and careful tasting stretch the small motion over time.
branches.cn: 慢喝与细品把这一小动作在时间上拉长。

branches.en: The small-amount idea transfers to spending, attention, and effort.
branches.cn: 「小量」的观念迁移到花钱、注意力与精力上。

branches.en: One draw of the lips becomes the countable measure.
branches.cn: 一次抿嘴成为可计量的单位。

branches.en: In the negative, the least sip means not even a little.
branches.cn: 在否定句里，「最小的一口」表示哪怕一点都不。

intro.en: Sip is a native imitative verb and builds few derived words: mainly sipped, sipping, and compounds such as sippy cup.
intro.cn: sip 是本土拟声动词，派生词很少：主要有 sipped、sipping 以及 sippy cup 这类复合说法。

latinIntro.en: Sip has no recorded Latin ancestor; its small-sucking sound may be imitative, and the linkage to Latin words is only uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: sip 没有可考的拉丁语来源；它的「小口吸」音或许只是拟声，与拉丁语词的关联并不确定。

items.example: Sip is first recorded in Middle English.
items.exampleCN: sip 最早见于中古英语文献。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms sipped, with a doubled p.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 sipped，并双写 p。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms sipping.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 sipping。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does it
items.example: The suffix -er forms sipper, one who takes small drinks.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 sipper，指小口喝的人。

items.example: The suffix -y forms sippy, as in sippy cup.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成 sippy，如 sippy cup（学饮杯）。

items.example: The noun sip appears from the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 名词 sip 自十六世纪起出现。

items.meaning: an event where drinks are sampled
items.example: Restaurants sometimes hold a sip-and-taste evening.
items.exampleCN: 餐厅有时会举办小口品饮之夜。

items.meaning: to drink a mouthful of the wrong thing
items.example: The prefix mis- builds the rare verb mis-sip.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mis- 构成罕见动词 mis-sip。

items.meaning: the act of taking small drinks
items.example: Sipping slowly keeps the drink warm.
items.exampleCN: 慢慢小口喝能让饮品保持温热。

definition_zh: 相当大的；可观的；大量的；宽阔的
definition_en: large enough to be noticed or to matter, especially in amount, extent or importance
core_image: 一只手摊开，比出一条够得着的宽度：那块东西大到占满整个手掌
scene: 比赛前夜，看台上陆续坐满观众，草坪上空回荡着欢呼。A sizeable crowd gathered outside the stadium before the final.
sceneCN: 这里 sizeable 是「相当大的」（第 1 个义项：数量大到足以引人注意）；句意：决赛前，体育场外聚集了一群规模相当大的观众。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词后缀 -able 得到的词干，义为「尺寸；大小」
size 加 -ed 构成，多用于复合词，义为「……尺寸的」，如 large sized
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「相当大地；可观地」

senses.title: Large in amount or number
senses.definition: large enough in number or quantity to be clearly noticed or to matter
senses.definitionCN: 数量或数目大到明显可见或足以产生影响
senses.example: A sizeable crowd gathered outside the stadium before the final.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛前，体育场外聚集了一大群人。
senses.why: Size grew out of assize, a session where values were assessed, so size is a measured amount; adding -able says the amount is enough to be reckoned with.
senses.whyCN: size 来自 assize（核定价值的会议），本质是被量出来的额度；再加 -able，就表示这份额度大到值得认真掂量。

senses.title: Large in physical extent
senses.definition: fairly big in area, volume or outward extent, especially of a room, building or piece of land
senses.definitionCN: 在面积、体积或外在规模上比较大，尤指房间、建筑或土地
senses.example: They moved into a sizeable room with windows on three sides.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬进了一间三面开窗的宽敞房间。
senses.why: The literal body sense keeps the plain picture of measurement: you can measure a room, so a room of marked extent is sizeable.
senses.whyCN: 字面本义保留了最朴素的测量画面：房间可以量，所以量出来面积可观，就是 sizeable。

senses.title: Important or considerable in effect
senses.definition: considerable in importance or effect, so that it can shape later events
senses.definitionCN: 在重要性或影响力上分量不轻，足以左右后来的事态
senses.example: The decision proved sizeable for the whole industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这一决定对整个行业影响不小。
senses.why: If an amount is big enough to be measured and noticed, it is also big enough to change outcomes, so sizeable moves from quantity to weight.
senses.whyCN: 数量既然大到能量、能被看见，也就大到能改变结果，于是 sizeable 从「数量」滑向「分量」。

senses.title: Of substantial money or value
senses.definition: amounting to a large sum of money or a valuable share, often in business or finance
senses.definitionCN: 达到一笔不小的金额或可观的份额，多用于商业和金融
senses.example: The firm holds a sizeable share of the local market.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在本地市场占有相当大的份额。
senses.why: Money is the most measurable amount of all, so the word settles naturally into phrases about sums, stakes and shares.
senses.whyCN: 钱是最好计量的一种量，因此这个词很自然地落在款项、股份与份额这类说法里。

intro.en: Sizeable is the adjective made from size with the suffix -able; size itself comes through Old French from the Latin word for a session, assidere.
intro.cn: sizeable 是 size 加形容词后缀 -able 构成的；size 则经由古法语溯源于拉丁语 assidere（坐在……旁边、落座）。

items.en: Assidere meant to sit beside, from ad- to and sedere to sit; from it came the courts and sessions that sat to decide matters.
items.cn: assidere 意为坐在旁边，由 ad-（向）与 sedere（坐）构成；由此派生出一系列开会、开庭的词。

items.en: Assise named a session held by court or council, and by extension the regulation or tax fixed in such a session.
items.cn: assise 指法院或议事会召开的一次会议，又引申为在这样的会上定下的规章或税额定费。

items.en: Assise came into English as assize, a session or an order setting standards, prices and amounts; the shorter form size was cut from it.
items.cn: 该词以 assize 进入英语，指一次会议或规定标准、价格与数额的法令；较短的 size 由它截短而来。

items.en: Size came to mean the fixed amount or magnitude of a thing, then the more familiar sense of how big something is.
items.cn: size 先指一件东西被规定下来的数额或大小，后来才成为今天熟悉的「尺寸、大小」之义。

items.en: Sized appears first in compounds such as middle sized; the ordinary word sizeable, built on size plus -able, is later and its exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: sized 最早见于 middle sized 这类复合词；由 size 加 -able 构成的常见词 sizeable 出现更晚，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The -e- between size and -able is simply a spelling bridge; American usage prefers the shorter sizable, and both spellings are standard.
items.cn: size 与 -able 之间的 e 只是拼写上的桥接；美式用法更常写 sizable，两种拼写都属规范。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the size family and words that merely look close; the near-meaning group gathers ordinary adjectives for quantities that are big.
note.cn: 形近组收 size 这一词族以及只是长得像的词；近义组收表示「数量大」的普通形容词，彼此语感有差异。

entries.definition: how big or small something is
entries.definitionCN: 基础名词，义为「尺寸；大小」

entries.definition: having a stated size, mostly in compounds
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「……尺寸的」，多用于复合词

entries.definition: able to be taken by force or by law
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可扣押的；可抓住的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: big in size or amount, plain and neutral
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「大的；大量的」，最平实、最中性

entries.definition: great enough to be noticed, often for amounts and effort
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，义为「相当大的；相当多的」，多用于数量与精力

entries.definition: large and solid, with a hint of real weight or value
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「可观的；实质性的」，暗含实在的分量与价值

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real assize history of size and the everyday phrases sizeable actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用 size 真实的 assize 词源，以及 sizeable 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Size began as a settled amount, so sizeable is simply an amount big enough to count.
normal.cn: size 本义是核定好的额度，所以 sizeable 就是大得数得清、算得上的那一份。

normal.en: The -able ending marks a threshold, not an exact figure: fairly big, though not enormous.
normal.cn: -able 这个词尾标记的是一条门槛而不是确切数字：比较大，但还不到巨大。

normal.en: A sizeable minority means a group too big to be dismissed.
normal.cn: a sizeable minority 指一群大到无法忽视的少数人。

normal.en: A sizeable sum is the phrase banks and newspapers use for real money.
normal.cn: a sizeable sum 是银行和报纸说到大笔款项时的常用说法。

normal.en: Compare large: large is bare and factual, while sizeable means large enough to be noticed.
normal.cn: 对比 large：large 只是平铺直叙，sizeable 强调「大到值得注意」。

abstract.en: Hold up an open hand to measure a crowd as it fills a square.
abstract.cn: 摊开手掌去量一片渐渐站满广场的人群。

abstract.en: Imagine a ruler laid across a room that is wider than the ruler itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺横放在一个比尺还宽的房间上。

abstract.en: See one heavy weight on a pan of a scale, tilting the beam with its consequence.
abstract.cn: 想象秤盘上放着一块沉甸甸的砝码，它的分量让横梁明显倾斜。

examples.en: A sizeable part of the budget went to new equipment.
examples.cn: 预算中有相当大一部分花在了新设备上。

examples.en: The town has attracted a sizable number of young families.
examples.cn: 这座小镇吸引了不少年轻家庭。

examples.en: She donated a sizeable sum to the flood relief fund.
examples.cn: 她向抗洪救灾基金捐了一笔可观的款项。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨伊泽」——一叠钱摊开，厚到捏不住边：数量可观；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 assidere（坐于旁边）→ 名词 assisa 指一次会议 → 古法语 assise（会议；会上定下的规章与数额）→ 英语 assize，后截短为 size（被核定的数额、大小）→ size + -able 构成 sizeable，核心义「数额大到值得掂量」。

sensesIntro.en: Sizeable always measures something up against a threshold: a number of people, a physical space, the weight of an effect, or an amount of money.
sensesIntro.cn: sizeable 始终在拿某个量跟一条门槛作比较：人数、空间、影响力的分量，或者一笔钱的数目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand measures a bulk that fills the whole palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的手掌去量一块大到占满掌心的东西。

branches.en: Counting people or things is the most common way the threshold is set.
branches.cn: 数人或数物，是最常见的设门槛方式。

branches.en: Measuring space keeps the oldest, most literal picture of size.
branches.cn: 量空间保留了 size 最老、最字面的画面。

branches.en: Weight of effect turns a quantity into influence.
branches.cn: 影响的分量把数量转成了影响力。

branches.en: Sums and shares are the amount line in business talk.
branches.cn: 款项与份额是商务话语里的金额线。

branches.en: Both are judged by a rough measure rather than an exact figure.
branches.cn: 两者都只凭粗略的估量判断，不求确切数字。

intro.en: Sizeable is an English-made adjective: the noun size plus the suffix -able, with sized as a shorter relative.
intro.cn: sizeable 是英语自造的形容词：名词 size 加后缀 -able，另有更短的近亲 sized。

latinIntro.en: The Latin words behind size are assidere and assisa, the sitting and the session; no separate Latin adjective existed for sizeable.
latinIntro.cn: size 背后的拉丁语词是 assidere（坐）与 assisa（会议），拉丁语中并没有与 sizeable 对应的形容词。

items.example: The prefix ad- appears in assidere, to sit beside.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ad- 出现在 assidere（坐在旁边）之中。

items.example: Sedere is also the root of session and sedate.
items.exampleCN: sedere 也是 session 与 sedate 的词根。

items.meaning: to sit beside, to sit in judgment
items.example: Assidere describes judges sitting together.
items.exampleCN: assidere 描述法官一起落座。

items.example: Assisa names the sitting and the amount it fixed.
items.exampleCN: assisa 既指会议，也指会议核定的数额。

items.example: Old French assise passed into English as assize.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 assise 进入英语成为 assize。

items.example: Size is the stem that sizeable is built on.
items.exampleCN: size 是构成 sizeable 的词干。

items.example: The suffix -able turns size into sizeable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把 size 变成 sizeable。

items.example: It forms the rare adverb sizably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成少用的副词 sizably。

items.example: It forms sized in compounds such as large sized.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 large sized 这类复合词中的 sized。

definition_zh: 怀疑者；持怀疑态度的人；怀疑论者；怀疑派哲学家
definition_en: a person who doubts claims that others accept, or who holds that certain knowledge is impossible
core_image: 一个人把额头凑近灯下，反复端详手里那块看似完美的石头，迟迟不肯点头
scene: 展销会上，销售员把一瓶保健品吹得天花乱坠，一位老人却皱着眉头，一再追问成分与实验数据。The old shopper was a skeptic about every new health product on the market.
sceneCN: 这里 skeptic 是「持怀疑态度的人」（第 1 个义项：不肯轻信一个说法的人）；句意：这位上了年纪的顾客对市场上每一种新保健品都抱怀疑态度。

pos.zh: 怀疑者；持怀疑态度的人；怀疑论者

collocations.zh: 对保健说法持怀疑的人

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「怀疑态度；怀疑论」；英式拼作 scepticism
由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「怀疑的」；英式拼作 sceptical
skeptical 再加 -ly 构成，义为「怀疑地」；英式拼作 sceptically

senses.title: A person who doubts a claim
senses.titleCN: 怀疑者；持怀疑态度的人
senses.definition: a person who is not convinced by a claim or an idea and asks for evidence before accepting it
senses.definitionCN: 对某个说法或观点不轻易相信、要求先看到证据才肯接受的人
senses.example: The old shopper was a skeptic about every new health product.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老顾客对每一种新保健品都持怀疑态度。
senses.why: Greek skeptikos means given to examining, from a verb meaning to look at closely; a skeptic is someone who keeps looking at a claim instead of nodding.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 skeptikos 意为「惯于审视的」，来自一个表示「细看」的动词；所以怀疑者就是那个看了又看、迟迟不点头的人。

senses.title: The philosophic school
senses.definition: a member of the ancient Greek school that withheld judgment because appearances can be weighed equally on both sides
senses.definitionCN: 古希腊的一个哲学流派成员，认为正反两面看起来同样有理，因此暂缓作出判断
senses.example: A Greek skeptic would suspend judgment rather than settle the question.
senses.exampleCN: 古希腊的怀疑论者宁愿暂缓判断，也不肯给问题下定论。
senses.why: The word was the name of that school before it was an everyday noun; philosophy keeps the oldest narrow sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先是那个哲学流派的名字，后来才成为日常用词；哲学里保留的正是它最早、最专门的意思。

senses.title: A doubter by temperament
senses.definition: a person whose usual habit is to question news, promises or arrangements and to expect them to fail
senses.definitionCN: 习惯上对新闻、承诺或安排抱有疑问、总觉得会出问题的人
senses.example: As a skeptic, he reads every glossy advertisement twice.
senses.exampleCN: 作为天性多疑的人，他每张漂亮的广告都要读两遍。
senses.why: The same examining gaze hardens into character, so skeptic can name a type of person rather than a single act of doubt.
senses.whyCN: 那种审视的目光一旦固化成性格，skeptic 就从「一次怀疑的动作」变成「一类人」。

senses.title: An opponent of a claimed trend
senses.titleCN: 对某种潮流或论断唱反调的人
senses.definition: a person who publicly disputes a widely reported trend, theory or prediction
senses.definitionCN: 公开对广为流传的趋势、理论或预测表示质疑的人
senses.example: The market skeptic doubted that the boom could last.
senses.exampleCN: 这位对市场持怀疑态度的人不相信繁荣能够持续。
senses.why: When a claim is shared by many, the one who examines it alone becomes the skeptic in the argument.
senses.whyCN: 当某个说法被众人接受时，单独去审视它的人就成了争论中的那位怀疑者。

intro.en: Skeptic comes from Greek skeptikos, given to examining, built on the noun skepsis, an act of looking carefully; the early English spelling sceptical kept the Greek k as c.
intro.cn: skeptic 来自希腊语 skeptikos，意为「惯于审视的」，源于名词 skepsis（仔细查看）；英语早期的写法 sceptical 把希腊字母 k 写成了 c。

items.en: Skeptikos meant given to examining or looking into something, from the noun skepsis. Its deeper origin is not settled, and the sources disagree on whether it is linked to scopein, to look at.
items.cn: skeptikos 意为「惯于审视、查究的」，源于名词 skepsis。更早的来源尚无定论，各家对它是否与 scopein（注视）同源看法不一。

items.en: Skeptikoi was the name given to philosophers who examined every argument and then suspended judgment; their school is called Pyrrhonism.
items.cn: skeptikoi 是对这样一批哲学家的称呼：他们审查一切论证，最后暂缓判断；这一流派后来称为皮浪主义。

items.en: Classical Latin borrowed it as scepticus, and sixteenth century French made sceptique; the exact French route may have come through the Latin word directly.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语借作 scepticus，十六世纪法语又造出 sceptique；法语这条路径是否直接来自拉丁语，不能完全确定。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the 1570s through French, first as a name for the ancient school, spelled sceptick, sceptic or skeptic.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪七十年代经由法语借入此词，最初是古代流派的名字，拼作 sceptick、sceptic 或 skeptic。

items.en: Skepticism and skeptical grow out of it, and the word widens from philosophy to anyone who doubts a claim.
items.cn: skepticism 与 skeptical 相继派生出来，词义也从哲学扩展到任何不相信某个说法的人。

items.en: Nineteenth century American spelling settled on skeptic, while British English kept sceptic, following the French and Latin c.
items.cn: 十九世纪美国拼写定为 skeptic；英式英语保留 sceptic，沿袭法语与拉丁语里的 c。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the spelling variants and the whole skepticism family; the near-meaning group gathers people who doubt, with different strength and tone.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写变体与整个 skepticism 词族；近义组收各种表达「不相信」的人，强度与语气各不相同。

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写，读音不变

entries.definition: doubtful about whether something is true
entries.definitionCN: 同词族形容词，义为「怀疑的」

entries.definition: an attitude of doubt, or the philosophical position
entries.definitionCN: 同词族名词，义为「怀疑态度；怀疑论」

entries.definition: someone who doubts, plain and unmarked
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「怀疑者」，最平实，不带学术色彩

entries.definition: someone who expects people to act only for themselves
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「愤世嫉俗者」，怀疑的是人的动机与品格

entries.definition: someone who does not accept a claim or a faith
entries.definitionCN: 较正式，义为「不信者」，比 skeptic 更绝对，常指不信某信仰

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek skepsis, the sceptic spelling history, and the phrases skeptic actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的希腊语 skepsis、sceptic 的拼写历史，以及 skeptic 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Skepsis is a close look, so a skeptic is someone still looking at the evidence.
normal.cn: skepsis 是「细看」，所以怀疑者就是仍在看证据的那个人。

normal.en: The Greek k became a c in sceptic, and American English later restored the k.
normal.cn: 希腊字母 k 在英式拼写里变成了 c，美式英语后来又把 k 恢复回来。

normal.en: A skeptic about something is the standard frame: a climate skeptic, a health skeptic.
normal.cn: 对某事持怀疑的人用这个框架表达：如气候怀疑者、保健质疑者。

normal.en: The whole family adds suffixes to the noun: skepticism, skeptical, skeptically.
normal.cn: 这一族都在名词后加词尾：skepticism、skeptical、skeptically。

normal.en: Compare cynic: a cynic distrusts people, a skeptic distrusts claims.
normal.cn: 对比 cynic：愤世嫉俗者不信人，怀疑者不信说法。

abstract.en: Watch a jeweller hold a stone up to the light again and again before nodding.
abstract.cn: 想象珠宝商把一颗石头举到灯前看了又看，才终于点头。

abstract.en: See two panes of glass, one for each side of an argument, turning equal in the light.
abstract.cn: 想象两块玻璃，分别映着争论的正反两面，在光下一样亮。

abstract.en: Picture a reader who folds down the corner of every promising paragraph.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者，把每一个看起来很诱人的段落都折了个角。

examples.en: Even a committed skeptic was surprised by the test results.
examples.cn: 就连一位一贯的怀疑者也被实验结果吓了一跳。

examples.en: She became a skeptic after reading two conflicting reports.
examples.cn: 读完两份互相矛盾的报道后，她变成了怀疑者。

examples.en: The skeptics asked for the raw data before opening their wallets.
examples.cn: 这些持怀疑态度的人要求先看到原始数据，才愿意掏钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死不提客」——你死不提任何证据，客人就只好一直怀疑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 skepsis（仔细查看）→ skeptikos（惯于审视的）→ 古希腊怀疑派名称 → 拉丁语 scepticus → 法语 sceptique → 英语 skeptic，核心义「把说法拿到眼前反复细看」。更早的来源尚无定论，一般认为与其相关而非同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Skeptic starts as the name of an ancient philosophic school, then names anyone who keeps examining a claim, then a doubting temperament, and finally a public opponent of a claimed trend.
sensesIntro.cn: skeptic 先是古代哲学流派的名字，然后指任何坚持审视某个说法的人，再指多疑的性格，最后指公开质疑某种潮流的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person holds an object up to the lamp and keeps examining it instead of nodding.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人把东西举到灯前，反复端详而不肯点头。

branches.en: Everyday doubt is the broad, common sense.
branches.cn: 日常的怀疑是宽泛、最常用的一层。

branches.en: The philosophic school is the oldest, narrowest sense.
branches.cn: 哲学流派是最早、最专门的一层。

branches.en: Habit turns a single act of doubt into a temperament.
branches.cn: 习惯把单次的怀疑固化成一种性格。

branches.en: Publicly opposing a trend puts the gaze into an argument.
branches.cn: 公开质疑某种潮流，把审视的目光放进了争论。

branches.en: One doubts a single claim, the other doubts by nature.
branches.cn: 一个怀疑的是某个具体说法，一个怀疑的是天性。

intro.en: Skeptic is a Greek noun kept almost whole through Latin and French, with the English family built by the suffixes -ism, -al and -ly.
intro.cn: skeptic 几乎整词从希腊语经拉丁语、法语传入英语，英语这一族靠 -ism、-al、-ly 等词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Classical Latin has the adjective scepticus but no separate verb of its own; the true root is the Greek noun skepsis.
latinIntro.cn: 古典拉丁语只有形容词 scepticus，没有自己的同源动词；真正的词根是希腊语名词 skepsis。

items.example: Skepsis gives the image of close looking.
items.exampleCN: skepsis 给出「细看」的画面。

items.example: The suffix -ikos forms the adjective skeptikos.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ikos 构成形容词 skeptikos。

items.example: Skeptikos was applied to the ancient doubters.
items.exampleCN: skeptikos 用来称呼古代的怀疑派。

items.meaning: of the sceptics, given to examining
items.example: Latin wrote the Greek k as c.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把希腊字母 k 写作 c。

items.example: French sceptique is the main gateway to English.
items.exampleCN: 法语 sceptique 是进入英语的主要通道。

items.example: The suffix -al forms skeptical.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 skeptical。

items.example: It forms skepticism, the attitude and the school.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 skepticism，既指态度也指学说。

items.example: It forms skeptically.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 skeptically。

items.example: The suffix -ic appears in the older spelling sceptick.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 见于较老的拼写 sceptick。

definition_zh: 使偏斜；歪曲；有偏斜的；倾斜的；偏斜度
definition_en: to make something slant or turn away from its true line, direction or balance, or to be slanted or distorted in that way
core_image: 一根本来笔直的指针被轻轻一推，歪出原来的方向，指向旁边
scene: 摄影师把相机斜着举起来又放下，抱怨地平线总是歪的。A slightly skew tripod made the horizon lean to the left.
sceneCN: 这里 skew 是「歪的、倾斜的」（第 2 个义项：偏离本来的直线或水平）；句意：一只略微歪斜的三脚架让地平线向左边倾斜。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「偏斜的；带偏差的」，用于数据和分布时指不对称
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「偏斜度」，统计学中指分布不对称的程度
一般认为由冠词 a- 与 skew 结合而成，义为「歪斜的；倾斜的」

senses.title: To distort results on purpose
senses.definition: to make statistics, results or an account lean towards one side and so give a false picture
senses.definitionCN: 使统计数据、结果或叙述偏向一方，从而给出失真的图景
senses.example: One pushy interviewer can skew the whole poll.
senses.exampleCN: 一个过于强势的访问员就可能让整份民意调查出现偏差。
senses.why: The word passed through Old Northern French escuier, to slip aside, so skew has always meant leaving the straight line; applied to numbers, that slip becomes a hidden pull towards one side.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经由古法语北方方言 escuier（滑到一边）而来，天生带着「离开直线」的意思；一旦用在数字上，这点滑移就变成了朝一边悄悄拉扯。

senses.title: Slanted out of line
senses.definition: at an angle rather than straight, true or level, as of a line, a picture or a surface
senses.definitionCN: 成角度而不正、不平、不直，多指线条、照片或表面
senses.example: The picture hung skew on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅画在墙上挂歪了。
senses.why: The physical sense is the clearest form of the core image: something that should be straight stands at an angle.
senses.whyCN: 物理义是核心意象最直观的形态：本该笔直的东西，却立在了一个角度上。

senses.title: Uneven in distribution
senses.definition: not spread evenly, so that values cluster on one side of a scale, a table or a graph
senses.definitionCN: 分布不均匀，数值聚集在量表、表格或图表的某一侧
senses.example: Income figures skew to the right in most countries.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数国家，收入数据呈右偏分布。
senses.why: A graph that leans to one side is literally a skewed graph, so statistics kept the visual tilt for uneven distributions.
senses.whyCN: 向一侧倾倒的图形在字面上就是歪的，统计学于是把这种视觉上的倾斜借用为「分布不对称」。

senses.title: To turn away or swerve
senses.definition: to turn away sharply from a straight path or direction, or to make a movement deviate from the intended line
senses.definitionCN: 从笔直的路线或方向猛然转开，或使某个动作偏离预定的路线
senses.example: The car skewed sideways on the wet road.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在湿滑的路面上侧向偏了出去。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer in the word: a motion that slips aside instead of going on straight.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层意思：一个动作没有直着往前，而是滑到了一边。

senses.title: The tilt itself
senses.definition: an angle, tilt or slant off the true line, as in a builder or a rail that is out of square
senses.definitionCN: 偏离正线的角度或倾斜，如建筑构件、轨道对不正
senses.example: A slight skew in the rail was enough to slow the trains.
senses.exampleCN: 铁轨上一点点的偏斜就足以让列车减速。
senses.why: The verb comes back as a noun: the angle produced by the slipping aside is itself the skew.
senses.whyCN: 动词又回到了名词：滑到一边所留下的那个角度，本身就是 skew。

intro.en: Skew is a rare case of a noun made out of a verb; the verb came into English from Old Northern French escuier, which itself goes back to the Latin verb exquadrare.
intro.cn: skew 属于少见的「由动词造成名词」的词；动词由古法语北方方言 escuier 进入英语，该词又可上溯到拉丁语动词 exquadrare。

items.en: Exquadrare meant to square off or make something square, built from ex-, out, and quadrus, a square.
items.cn: exquadrare 意为削成方形、使方正，由 ex-（向外）与 quadrus（方块）构成。

items.en: In Old French the word became escuier, to slip aside or turn off; the spelling and exact form in Northern French are uncertain.
items.cn: 在古法语中该词变为 escuier，意为滑开、偏向一边；其北方方言的具体拼写与形式尚不确定。

items.en: The noun skew is recorded in English in the fifteenth century in the sense of a slipping movement; the exact first date is unsure.
items.cn: 名词 skew 在英语中以「滑开的动作」之义见于记录，一般认为在十五世纪；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The verb skew, to slip aside, is recorded from about the sixteenth century; its link to the Old Northern French word is generally accepted, though the sources date the borrowing somewhat differently.
items.cn: 动词 skew（滑到一边）约在十六世纪有记录；一般认为它来自古法语北方方言词，但各家所给年代略有出入。

items.en: Skew settles into the technical language of building, sewing and printing for lines and tools that are not square.
items.cn: skew 进入建筑、缝纫与印刷等行业的专门语汇，用来指不正方的线条与工具。

items.en: Nineteenth century statistics gave skewness and skewed numbers the sense of uneven distributions, a sense now standard in science and journalism.
items.cn: 十九世纪统计学使 skewness 与 skewed 有了「分布不均匀」之义，如今这一用法在科学与新闻中已属常规。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the skew root or merely the same outline; the near-meaning group gathers words for leaning, turning aside and distorting.
note.cn: 形近组收与 skew 同根或外形相近的词；近义组收表示「倾斜、偏开、歪曲」的词，各有自己的使用场合。

entries.definition: not straight, twisted to one side
entries.definitionCN: 同根，义为「歪斜的；倾斜的」，多作表语

entries.definition: slanted or showing a systematic bias
entries.definitionCN: 派生形容词，义为「偏斜的；存在系统偏差的」

entries.definition: a long pin that holds meat together
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「烤肉签」；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to lean at an angle, often neutral
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「倾斜」，语气中性，不带「失真」的含义

entries.definition: to slope or tip, usually by a noticeable amount
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「倾斜、翘起」，多指明显地向一边倾倒

entries.definition: to twist facts or a shape out of its true form
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「扭曲、歪曲」，强调把事实或形状整个扭变形

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real exquadrare history of the root and the phrases skew mostly appears in today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用这个词根真实的 exquadrare 历史，以及 skew 如今最常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ex- plus quadrus meant out of square, so anything skew is no longer square.
normal.cn: ex- 加 quadrus 本义就是「离开方块」，所以凡是 skew 的东西都不再方正。

normal.en: Askew is the same word with a worn-down a- in front.
normal.cn: askew 就是同一个词前面磨出了一个 a-。

normal.en: Skewed data misrepresents a whole group, which is why the phrase skew the results matters so much.
normal.cn: skewed data 会让整个群体被误读，这正是 skew the results 这句话重要的原因。

normal.en: In statistics a skewed distribution has an uneven tail on one side.
normal.cn: 在统计学里，偏态分布就是某一侧拖着一条不对称的长尾。

normal.en: Compare slant: to slant something is to set it at an angle, to skew it is to make that angle change the picture.
normal.cn: 对比 slant：slant 只是把东西摆在斜角上，skew 则让这个斜角改变了判断。

abstract.en: A survey table is quietly balanced on one raised leg, so every bar leans the same way.
abstract.cn: 一张调查表被一条垫高的桌腿悄悄支起，所有柱子都朝同一个方向歪。

abstract.en: A framer puts a nail to the wall, steps back and sees the frame hang crooked.
abstract.cn: 装框的人钉好钉子，退后一看，画框斜挂着。

abstract.en: See a column of numbers with a long tail dragging far to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字右侧拖着一条很长的尾巴。

examples.en: Rising food prices skew the inflation figures.
examples.cn: 食品价格上涨使通胀数据出现偏差。

examples.en: The new tax scale skews the burden towards higher earners.
examples.cn: 新的税率档让负担偏向高收入者。

examples.en: The chart shows a skewed distribution with a long tail on the right.
examples.cn: 这张图呈现的是一个右侧长尾的偏态分布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四-Q」——字母 Q 没摆正，成了歪的口：偏斜、歪曲；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 exquadrare（削成方形，由 ex- 与 quadrus 方块构成）→ 古法语 escuier（滑开、偏向）→ 英语 skew，核心义「离开正方、滑向一边」。

sensesIntro.en: Skew begins with slipping aside and grows in two directions: a slanted line or motion, and a slanted picture whose numbers lean the wrong way.
sensesIntro.cn: skew 从「滑向一边」出发，分成两条路：一条是线条与动作的倾斜，另一条是数据与说法被带偏、失真。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight needle is nudged aside and points away from the true line.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔直的指针被一推，歪出原线，指向旁边。

branches.en: When numbers lean, skew is done on purpose and the result is false.
branches.cn: 数字被带偏时，skew 是人为的，结果也随之失真。

branches.en: The angle that a line or object takes is both the adjective and the noun.
branches.cn: 线条或物件所成的角度，既是形容词义也是名词义。

branches.en: Statistics drew an even histogram with one side dragged long.
branches.cn: 统计学画出一张笔直的直方图，只是一侧被拖长。

branches.en: The earliest motion sense keeps the slipping image in plain view.
branches.cn: 最早的动作义仍把「滑开」的画面留在明处。

branches.en: A skewed sample and a skewed distribution both pull a curve away from its centre.
branches.cn: 偏斜的样本与偏态分布，都把曲线从中心拽向一边。

intro.en: Skew keeps the shape of a Latin verb, ex- plus the square root quadrus, and English adds -ed and -ness to make its family.
intro.cn: skew 保留了拉丁语动词的构形：ex- 前缀加表「方块」的词根 quadrus；英语再用 -ed 与 -ness 扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin quadrus, square, is the root; ex- adds the idea of out of or away from, and exquadrare is attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quadrus（方块）是词根，ex- 加「在外、离开」的意思，exquadrare 有文献记录。

items.example: Ex- marks moving away from the square.
items.exampleCN: ex- 标出「离开方块」的动作。

items.example: Quadrus gives the square that the word starts from.
items.exampleCN: quadrus 给出这个词出发时的那块方形。

items.example: Exquadrare is the Latin verb behind the French word.
items.exampleCN: exquadrare 是法语词背后的拉丁语动词。

items.meaning: to slip aside, to turn off
items.example: Escuier is the direct known source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: escuier 是英语动词已知的直接来源。

items.example: Skew claims to come from the Old Northern French word.
items.exampleCN: skew 被认为来自古法语北方方言的那个词。

items.example: It appears in askew, leaning to one side.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 askew（偏斜的）之中。

items.example: It forms skewed and its statistical sense.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 skewed 及其统计学的意义。

items.example: It forms skewness, the measure of asymmetry.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 skewness，即衡量不对称程度的量。

items.example: It forms skewer, which is a long pin, and it only looks alike.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 skewer（烤肉签），这个词只是与目标词长得像。

definition_zh: 用料不足的；短小的；吝啬的；不足的
definition_en: made with too little material or too little of something, so that it barely covers or barely satisfies
core_image: 一件布太少、边角短到勉强遮身的衣服
scene: 宴席上的菜色还算齐整，可每只盘子里的分量都少得让人不好意思再夹。The host served a skimpy dinner that left every guest hungry.
sceneCN: 这里 skimpy 是「分量少、给得不够」（第 1 个义项：用料的量不足）；句意为主人准备了一顿分量寒酸的晚餐，每位客人都没吃饱。

pos.zh: 形容词：用料不足的；尺寸小到勉强遮住的；吝啬的；不够用的

derivatives.zh: 由词根直接构成的动词，义为「吝惜；省着用」
由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「吝啬地；用得过少地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「料少；吝啬」

senses.title: Made with too little material
senses.definition: made or given with too little of something, so that it is barely enough
senses.definitionCN: 用极少材料做成或给得很少，刚好够或根本不够
senses.example: The hotel gave us a skimpy breakfast of one roll and weak coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店给我们的早餐少得可怜，只有一个小面包和淡咖啡。
senses.why: Skimp is a verb of scrimping and stinting, so skimpy describes anything made by short-measure saving.
senses.whyCN: skimp 是表示「省着用、吝惜」的动词，所以 skimpy 形容任何因抠着用料而做出来的东西。

senses.title: Cut short in size
senses.definition: cut very short and narrow, so that it covers much less of the body than usual
senses.definitionCN: 又短又窄，遮住的身体部位比通常少得多
senses.example: She wore a skimpy top and shorts on the hottest day of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 在全年最热的一天，她穿了一件短小的上衣和短裤。
senses.why: A garment made with little cloth is short by nature, so the material-saving sense turns into a visual one.
senses.whyCN: 用少量布做成的衣服天然就短，于是「省料」的意思自然长出了视觉上的「短小」。

senses.title: Reluctant to spend
senses.definition: unwilling to give or spend money, effort or information
senses.definitionCN: 不愿拿出钱财、精力或信息
senses.example: My uncle is skimpy with praise but generous with advice.
senses.exampleCN: 我叔叔极少夸奖别人，却乐于给人建议。
senses.why: From measuring out cloth to measuring out money, the same habit of holding back spreads to everything given.
senses.whyCN: 从计算布料扩展到计算钱物，这份「不舍得给」的习惯蔓延到一切给予之事。

senses.title: Too little for what is needed
senses.definition: not enough in amount, detail or quality for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、细节或质量上达不到某个目的所需的水平
senses.example: We cannot plan a whole trip with such skimpy details.
senses.exampleCN: 信息这么不足，我们无法规划整趟旅行。
senses.why: When a thing is made short measure, it always falls short of the demand, so skimpy becomes a general word for insufficiency.
senses.whyCN: 凡是被抠着做出来的东西总会达不到需求，于是 skimpy 变成了泛指「不足」的词。

intro.en: Skimpy is first recorded in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth century as the adjective of skimp, a verb of scrimping and stinting whose own origin is uncertain.
