intro.cn: skimpy 首见于十八世纪末到十九世纪初，是动词 skimp（省着用、吝惜）的形容词形式，而 skimp 的来源本身尚不确定。

items.en: The verb skimp appears in the seventeenth century as a familiar word of scrimping; no certain earlier source is known.
items.cn: 动词 skimp 在十七世纪已作口语词出现，义为省着用；更早的确定来源未知。

items.en: Skimp means to give less than is needed, to stint on food, cloth or effort.
items.cn: skimp 意为给得比需要的少，在食物、布料或用力上节省。

items.en: The adjective skimpy is formed with the common suffix -y and first means niggardly and meagre.
items.cn: 形容词 skimpy 由常见后缀 -y 构成，最初意为吝啬的、匮乏的。

items.en: Skimpy extends from portions and rations to clothing cut too short.
items.cn: skimpy 从食物分量扩展到裁剪过短的衣物。

items.en: Modern English uses skimpy for budgets, details and information as well as clothes.
items.cn: 现代英语把 skimpy 用于预算、细节和信息，而不再限于衣物。

note.en: Skimpy belongs to a small scrimping family with skimp and skimpily, and sits close to meagre, scant and scanty.
note.cn: skimpy 属于 skimp、skimpily 这一小族「省着用」的词，并与 meagre、scant、scanty 意义相近。

entries.definition: to remove a layer from the surface of a liquid
entries.definitionCN: 撇去液体表面的浮物；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: with the fat or cream taken from the top
entries.definitionCN: 撇过脂的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to spend as little as possible
entries.definitionCN: 精打细算；只是拼写相近，一般认为词源与 skimp 不同

entries.definition: small in quantity and poor in quality
entries.definitionCN: 少量的；贫乏的

entries.definition: too little in amount; barely enough
entries.definitionCN: 欠缺的；勉强够的

entries.definition: unwilling to give or spend
entries.definitionCN: 吝啬的

normalIntro.en: Skimpy is the adjective of skimp: measure out less than you should, and everything you make will look thin.
normalIntro.cn: skimpy 是 skimp 的形容词：该给的量偏要少给，做出来的东西自然处处单薄。

normal.en: To skimp is to give too little, and skimpy is what the result looks like.
normal.cn: skimp 是给得太少，skimpy 就是那副单薄的样子。

normal.en: The suffix -y turns a verb into an adjective, as in smelly from smell and risky from risk.
normal.cn: 后缀 -y 把动词变成形容词，如 smell 变 smelly、risk 变 risky。

normal.en: Skimpy clothing is short because too little cloth went into it.
normal.cn: skimpy 的衣服之所以短，是因为用料太少。

normal.en: Skimpiness is the noun, formed with the suffix -ness.
normal.cn: skimpiness 是名词，由后缀 -ness 构成。

normal.en: Compare meagre and scanty: skimpy often brings in a hint of stinginess.
normal.cn: 对比 meagre 与 scanty：skimpy 常多一层「抠门」的味道。

abstract.en: Picture a baker cutting one loaf into sixteen thin slices so it will last the week.
abstract.cn: 想象面包师把一个面包切成十六片薄片，好让它撑过一周。

abstract.en: Imagine a summer top made from a single narrow strip of cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一件夏天的上衣只用一条窄布做成。

abstract.en: Think of a coin held so tightly that the hand will not open.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币被握得死紧，手掌怎么也张不开。

examples.en: The players complained about their skimpy meals on the long tour.
examples.cn: 球员们抱怨长途巡游期间饭菜分量太少。

examples.en: That skirt is rather skimpy for a job interview.
examples.cn: 那条裙子对求职面试来说太短小了。

examples.en: The report was skimpy on figures and full of vague praise.
examples.cn: 那份报告数据少得可怜，满是空泛的赞誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯金皮」——「斯」是斤斤计较的省，省到最后只剩「皮」，皮包骨头就是 skimpy；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 动词 skimp（省着用；吝惜）加形容词后缀 -y 构成，skimp 的来源不确定，一般认为与英语中表「削减、克扣」的口语词有关，暂无可靠的拉丁或日耳曼语同源词。

sensesIntro.en: Skimpy starts from material given short measure, passes to clothing that covers too little, then to a stingy nature, and ends as a general word for anything insufficient.
sensesIntro.cn: skimpy 从「用料被克扣」起步，转到遮得太少的衣物，再扩展为吝啬的性情，最后泛指一切不够用的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short dress cut from too little cloth.
core.cn: 核心意象：用太少布料裁出来的短衣。

branches.en: Too little material makes a meal or a portion look mean.
branches.cn: 用料不足，让一顿饭或一份食物显得寒酸。

branches.en: Little cloth means a short cut, so the word turns visual.
branches.cn: 布少就裁得短，词义因此变为视觉上的「短小」。

branches.en: The habit of holding back becomes a moral judgement about money.
branches.cn: 舍不得给的习惯，变成对钱财的品性评价。

branches.en: Anything given short measure falls short of the demand.
branches.cn: 凡是被抠着给的，都会达不到需求。

branches.en: A skimpy budget and skimpy details are both short of what is needed.
branches.cn: 拮据的预算与稀少的细节，都是不敷所需。

intro.en: Skimpy is built on the English verb skimp plus the adjective suffix -y, with a small family of skimping words around it.
intro.cn: skimpy 由英语动词 skimp 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，周围有一小族表示「克扣」的词。

latinIntro.en: Skimp has no accepted Latin source, so there are no Latin relatives to list here.
latinIntro.cn: skimp 没有公认的拉丁语来源，因此这里没有可列的拉丁语同源词。

items.meaning: to stint, to give too little
items.example: Skimp is the verb at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: skimp 是这个词族的动词核心。

items.meaning: forming adjectives meaning full of or having
items.meaningCN: 构成形容词，表示「多……的、有……性质的」
items.example: The suffix -y turns skimp into skimpy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 skimp 变成 skimpy。

items.example: Skimpy describes clothes and portions alike.
items.exampleCN: skimpy 既能形容衣服，也能形容食物分量。

items.example: The adverb skimpily is formed with -ly.
items.exampleCN: 副词 skimpily 由后缀 -ly 构成。

items.meaningCN: 构成表性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness forms skimpiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 skimpiness。

items.example: Skimpiness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: skimpiness 指这种性质本身。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词比较级的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er forms skimpier.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成比较级 skimpier。

items.example: Skimpier compares two outfits.
items.exampleCN: skimpier 用于比较两件衣服。

items.example: Skimping on safety costs lives later.
items.exampleCN: 在安全上省工省料，日后要付出生命的代价。

definition_zh: 跳过；略过；跳绳；蹦跳；跳级
definition_en: to move quickly over the surface with little jumps, or to pass over something on purpose
core_image: 脚尖在石板上一连两次轻点，像打水漂一样一闪而过
scene: 放学铃响后，孩子们在操场上甩起绳子，一个接一个地跳。The girls took turns skipping while the boys counted the jumps.
sceneCN: 这里 skip 是「跳绳」（第 4 个义项：跳绳这种连续跳跃的动作）；句意为女孩们轮流跳绳，男孩们数着跳的次数。

pos.zh: 动词：跳过；略过；跳绳；蹦跳；跳级
名词：跳跃；遗漏；（英）跳过的容器

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成的名词，义为「跳绳」
形似本词，义为「船长；队长」；一般认为只是拼写相近，词源与 skip 无关
形似本词，义为「鲣鱼」；一般认为只是拼写相近，词源与 skip 无关

senses.title: To pass over something on purpose
senses.definition: to fail to do, use, take or mention something, usually because it is not important or not wanted
senses.definitionCN: 未做、未用、未取或未提及某事，通常因为它不重要或不需要
senses.example: You can skip the first chapter if you are short of time.
senses.exampleCN: 如果时间不够，你可以跳过第一章。
senses.why: Skip names a leap that goes over a surface without settling on it, so an item is simply passed over.
senses.whyCN: “跳过”本义是在表面上跃过而不落定，所以在清单里被跳过就是“略过”。

senses.title: To leave out by accident
senses.definition: to omit or leave something out without meaning to
senses.definitionCN: 无意中省去或遗漏了某物
senses.example: The editor accidentally skipped a line of the poem.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑不小心漏掉了诗中的一行。
senses.why: When the eye or the hand leaps without intending it, the place it never touched becomes a gap.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛或手不自觉地一跃，没碰到的位置就留下空缺，于是发生了遗漏。

senses.title: To miss something one should attend
senses.definition: to fail to attend a class, a meal or an event
senses.definitionCN: 没有去上课、吃饭或参加某个活动
senses.example: He skipped lunch to finish the report.
senses.exampleCN: 他为了写完报告没吃午饭。
senses.why: Not touching a thing at all is the extreme case of passing over it: you are simply elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 完全不碰某物，是“掠过”的极端情形：你人在别处，于是缺席。

senses.title: To move with light hops
senses.definition: to move forward with small quick jumps, or to jump over a rope that is being turned
senses.definitionCN: 用小而快的跳跃前进，或跳正在被抡动的绳子
senses.example: The child skipped down the garden path.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子蹦蹦跳跳地沿着花园小径去了。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the light hopping step, alive in rope skipping and children games.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是轻快跳跃，在跳绳与儿童游戏中一直延续。

senses.title: To advance fast over an edge
senses.definition: to bounce quickly off a surface, as a flat stone does across water
senses.definitionCN: 像扁石子擦过水面那样，在表面上快速反弹着前进
senses.example: He made the stone skip four times across the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 他让石子在水塘上跳了四下。
senses.why: The bouncing stone shows the same leap, now horizontal, skimming a surface it never enters.
senses.whyCN: 弹跳的石子呈现同一跃动，只是方向变成横向，擦过它从未进入的水面。

intro.en: Skip is recorded in Middle English and is generally thought to come from a northern Germanic verb meaning to spring or dart, though the exact source is disputed.
intro.cn: skip 见于中古英语，一般认为来自北方日耳曼语中表示「弹起、疾冲」的动词，但确切来源仍有争议。

items.en: A verb skip appears meaning to leap or spring lightly, first recorded in northern texts.
items.cn: 动词 skip 出现，意为轻快地跳跃或弹起，最早见于英格兰北部文献。

items.en: The word is compared with Middle Dutch and Low German springing words, but no single source is certain.
items.cn: 这个词常与中古荷兰语、低地德语中表「弹跳」的词相比较，但没有唯一确定的来源。

items.en: Skip also means to pass over or hurry past, which grows into the sense of leaving something out.
items.cn: skip 又表示「越过、匆匆经过」，并由此发展出「略去」的意思。

items.en: Skipping with a rope is recorded as a children game and later becomes physical exercise.
items.cn: 跳绳被记录下来，先是儿童游戏，后来成为体育运动。

items.en: Modern English adds skip class, skip a grade, skip breakfast and skip a track.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出逃课、跳级、不吃早饭以及跳过曲目等用法。

note.en: Skip covers both leaping and leaving out, and sits beside jump, hop and omit in meaning while sharing spelling with skim.
note.cn: skip 既表示跳跃又表示略去，在意义上与 jump、hop、omit 相邻，在拼写上又与 skim 相近。

entries.definitionCN: 掠过；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definitionCN: 单脚跳；小跳

normalIntro.en: Skip keeps one image for two ideas: a light step that carries you past something without touching it.
normalIntro.cn: skip 用一个意象贯通两层意思：轻轻一跃，不碰地面就从某物上方掠过。

normal.en: Skip over a problem and you have left it out; skip a class and you have left it behind.
normal.cn: skip over 一个难题就是把它略过；skip a class 就是不上这节课。

normal.en: The double p in skipped and skipping keeps the short vowel of skip.
normal.cn: skipped 与 skipping 双写 p，是为了保持 skip 的短元音。

normal.en: Skip and skim are both quick-reading words: skim runs the eye, skip jumps a piece.
normal.cn: skip 与 skim 都是快速阅读的词：skim 是眼睛扫过去，skip 是整段跳过去。

normal.en: Skipping rope is called skipping in Britain and jump rope in America.
normal.cn: 跳绳在英式英语中说 skipping，在美式英语中说 jump rope。

normal.en: Compare omit and miss: skip is the most informal and most active of the three.
normal.cn: 对比 omit 与 miss：skip 三者中最口语、最有「主动跳开」的动感。

abstract.en: Picture a stone bouncing twice over a pond before it sinks.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子在水塘上弹了两下才沉下去。

abstract.en: Imagine a reader flicking past one paragraph with a finger.
abstract.cn: 想象读者用手指一拨，把一段文字翻了过去。

abstract.en: Think of an empty chair at the breakfast table.
abstract.cn: 想象早餐桌上空着的一把椅子。

examples.en: She skipped her usual coffee to catch the early train.
examples.cn: 她没喝平日的咖啡，赶去乘早班车。

examples.en: The pupils skip rope in the yard every morning.
examples.cn: 学生们每天早上在院子里跳绳。

examples.en: He skipped over the boring pages and jumped to the ending.
examples.cn: 他略过那些乏味的页码，直接翻到了结尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死记不」——死记不下来，就干脆「跳」过去，跳过一段再看；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语动词 skip（轻跳、弹起），一般认为来自北方日耳曼语中表「弹起、疾冲」的动词，来源不确定；先有「跳跃」，后引申为「越过、略去」。

sensesIntro.en: Skip starts with a light spring, which first turns into passing over a thing, then leaving it out, then missing an event, and finally the literal skipping of a rope or a stone.
sensesIntro.cn: skip 从轻轻一跃开始，先引申为从某物上掠过，再引申为把它略去、缺席某事，最后回到字面上的跳绳与打水漂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone that hops twice over water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗在睡眠似的湖面上弹跳两次的石子。

branches.en: Passing over a step on purpose becomes the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 有意从某个步骤上方掠过，成为最常见的义项。

branches.en: The same leap without intent produces a gap and a missed item.
branches.cn: 同样的跳跃若不带意图，就会留下缺口和遗漏之物。

branches.en: Not touching a thing at all means being absent from it.
branches.cn: 完全不碰某物，就等于缺席于它。

branches.en: The literal hop returns in children games and rope skipping.
branches.cn: 字面上的跳跃在儿童游戏与跳绳中重新出现。

branches.en: A child hops on the path; a stone hops on the water.
branches.cn: 孩子在小径上蹦跳，石子在水面上弹跳。

intro.en: Skip is a short Germanic verb with few true affixes; its family is built with -ed, -ing and the noun -ing.
intro.cn: skip 是简短的日耳曼语动词，真正的词缀很少，词族主要由 -ed、-ing 和名词化用法构成。

latinIntro.en: Skip has no accepted Latin source, so there are no Latin relatives to list here.
latinIntro.cn: skip 没有公认的拉丁语来源，因此这里没有可列的拉丁语同源词。

items.exampleCN: skipping 是这项运动的英式叫法。
